    6: // liveness) lives in `packages/credits` and was integration-tested in phases
    7: // 2â€“3 BEFORE this UI existed (skill B7). Nothing is re-decided here.
    8: //
    9: // FAILURE CHANNEL: a server action's only way back to a server-rendered page is
   10: // the URL, so a refusal redirects with a short CODE and the page owns the words
   11: // (see ../../billing-errors.ts for why not the message). The raw error is
   12: // logged server-side, which is where its ids and instants belong.
   13: import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
   14: import { requireUser } from "@respin/auth";
   15: import { respinDb } from "@respin/db";
   16: import { respinCredits } from "@respin/credits/app-server";
   17: import { rethrowNextControlFlow } from "../../../../lib/next-control-flow";
   18: import {
   19:   AppBaseUrlMissingError,
   20:   billingErrorCode,
   21:   type BillingErrorCode,
   22: } from "../../billing-errors";
   23: 
   24: const BILLING_PATH = "/settings/billing";
   25: 
   26: /**
   27:  * Where a refusal may send the reader. An ALLOWLIST, not the raw `from` field:
   28:  * a form value that reaches `redirect()` unchecked is an open redirect.
   29:  *
   30:  * A `Set`, not an object map, deliberately: `RETURN_PATHS[raw]` on a plain
   31:  * object answers for `"__proto__"` and `"constructor"` too, and `?? fallback`
   32:  * would not catch it â€” a crafted `from=constructor` would have handed
   33:  * `redirect()` a function.
   34:  */
   35: const RETURN_PATHS = new Set<string>(["/usage", BILLING_PATH]);
   36: 
   37: function returnPathOf(formData: FormData | null): string {
   38:   const raw = formData ? String(formData.get("from") ?? "") : "";
   39:   return RETURN_PATHS.has(raw) ? raw : BILLING_PATH;
   40: }
   41: 
   42: function failHref(err: unknown, formData: FormData | null): string {
   43:   const code: BillingErrorCode = billingErrorCode(err);
   44:   console.error(`[billing-action] refused (${code})`, err);
   45:   return `${returnPathOf(formData)}?e=${encodeURIComponent(code)}`;
   46: }
   47: 
   48: /**
   49:  * TWO mechanisms keep a gate from being swallowed, and both are needed:
   50:  *
   51:  *  1. `requireUser()` is called ABOVE the try in every action below. It signals
   52:  *     "no session" by THROWING a `redirect()` â€” a plain `Error` carrying
   53:  *     `digest: "NEXT_REDIRECT;â€¦"` â€” so calling it inside the try meant an
   54:  *     expired session on an open billing form was logged
   55:  *     `[billing-action] refused (unknown)` and sent to
   56:  *     `/settings/billing?e=unknown` instead of `/sign-in`
   57:  *     (billing/tenancy round-2 CHANGE 1).
   58:  *  2. Every catch below re-throws Next's control flow as its FIRST statement
   59:  *     (`lib/next-control-flow.ts`), enforced by a source scan over app/** and
   60:  *     lib/** in `tests/action-gate.test.ts`. Hoisting alone fixes the seven
   61:  *     call sites that exist today; the scan is what stops M2 adding an eighth.
   62:  *
   63:  * `withWorkspace` stays INSIDE the try on purpose: `WorkspaceAccessError` is a
   64:  * domain refusal with its own rendered copy (`workspace_access`), not a
   65:  * navigation signal.
   66:  */
   67: /**
   68:  * Absolute URLs for Stripe to return to. `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is already the
   69:  * app's own base URL (env.example), so this adds no new configuration â€” and it
   70:  * REFUSES rather than guessing a host, because a guessed success_url sends a
   71:  * paying customer to a page that does not exist.
   72:  */
   73: function appBaseUrl(): string {
   74:   const base = process.env.BETTER_AUTH_URL;
   75:   if (!base) throw new AppBaseUrlMissingError();
   76:   return base.replace(/\/+$/, "");
   77: }
   78: 
   79: function checkoutUrls() {
   80:   const base = appBaseUrl();
   81:   return {
   82:     successUrl: `${base}/usage`,
   83:     cancelUrl: `${base}${BILLING_PATH}`,
   84:   };
   85: }
   86: 
   87: export async function subscribeAction(formData: FormData): Promise<void> {
   88:   // THE GATE, above the try. Its refusal is a redirect, i.e. a throw.
   89:   const user = await requireUser();
   90:   let url: string;
   91:   try {
   92:     const tier = String(formData.get("tier") ?? "");
   93:     if (tier !== "creator" && tier !== "pro" && tier !== "studio") {
   94:       throw new Error(`unknown tier "${tier}"`);
   95:     }
   96:     const scope = await respinDb.withWorkspace({ authUserId: user.id });
   97:     url = await respinCredits.createTierCheckoutUrl(
   98:       scope,
   99:       tier,
  100:       user.email,
  101:       checkoutUrls()
  102:     );
  103:   } catch (err) {
  104:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
  105:     redirect(failHref(err, formData));
  106:   }
  107:   redirect(url);
  108: }
  109: 
  110: export async function buyPackAction(formData: FormData): Promise<void> {
  111:   const user = await requireUser();
  112:   let url: string;
  113:   try {
  114:     const scope = await respinDb.withWorkspace({ authUserId: user.id });
  115:     url = await respinCredits.createPackCheckoutUrl(
  116:       scope,
  117:       user.email,
  118:       checkoutUrls()
  119:     );
  120:   } catch (err) {
  121:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
  122:     redirect(failHref(err, formData));
  123:   }
  124:   redirect(url);
  125: }
  126: 
  127: export async function openPortalAction(formData: FormData): Promise<void> {
  128:   const user = await requireUser();
  129:   let url: string;
  130:   try {
  131:     const scope = await respinDb.withWorkspace({ authUserId: user.id });
  132:     url = await respinCredits.createPortalUrl(
  133:       scope,
  134:       `${appBaseUrl()}${BILLING_PATH}`
  135:     );
  136:   } catch (err) {
  137:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
  138:     redirect(failHref(err, formData));
  139:   }
  140:   redirect(url);
  141: }
  142: 
  143: export async function pauseAction(formData: FormData): Promise<void> {
  144:   const user = await requireUser();
  145:   try {
  146:     const scope = await respinDb.withWorkspace({ authUserId: user.id });
  147:     // Number(), not a bounded union: the range is CONFIG (`pauseMonths`), and
  148:     // the package validates against the active version. A type-level 1|2|3 here
  149:     // would be a second, un-versioned authority.
  150:     await respinCredits.pauseSubscription(scope, Number(formData.get("months")));
  151:   } catch (err) {
  152:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
  153:     redirect(failHref(err, formData));
  154:   }
  155:   redirect(returnPathOf(formData));
  156: }
  157: 
  158: export async function resumeAction(formData: FormData): Promise<void> {
  159:   const user = await requireUser();
  160:   try {
  161:     const scope = await respinDb.withWorkspace({ authUserId: user.id });
  162:     await respinCredits.resumeSubscription(scope);
  163:   } catch (err) {
  164:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
  165:     redirect(failHref(err, formData));
  166:   }
  167:   redirect(returnPathOf(formData));
  168: }
  169: 
  170: export async function setAutoTopupAction(formData: FormData): Promise<void> {
  171:   const user = await requireUser();
  172:   try {
  173:     const scope = await respinDb.withWorkspace({ authUserId: user.id });
  174:     const enabled = formData.get("enabled") !== null;
  175:     // Dollars in the form, CENTS in the domain (the cap is compared against
  176:     // real charged amounts). A blank or non-numeric field becomes NaN, which
  177:     // the package refuses with AutoTopupCapError â€” one validator, not two.
  178:     const capUsd = Number(String(formData.get("capUsd") ?? ""));
  179:     await respinCredits.setAutoTopup(scope, {
  180:       enabled,
  181:       monthlyCapCents: enabled ? Math.round(capUsd * 100) : undefined,
  182:     });
  183:   } catch (err) {
  184:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
  185:     redirect(failHref(err, formData));
  186:   }
  187:   redirect(returnPathOf(formData));
  188: }
===== respin/app/(product)/settings/billing/page.tsx =====
    1: // /settings/billing â€” REQ-G01/G03/G08 UI half, owner-gated at REQ-A02.
    2: // Server component: gate, scope, read, render. Every mutation is a server
    3: // action in ./actions.ts, and every rule those actions enforce lives in
    4: // packages/credits (skill B7: the money paths were integration-tested in
    5: // phases 2â€“3, before this page existed).
    6: import { requireUser } from "@respin/auth";
    7: import { respinDb } from "@respin/db";
    8: import {
    9:   hasLiveStripeSubscription,
   10:   isStripeConfigured,
   11:   respinCredits,
   12: } from "@respin/credits/app-server";
   13: import { getActiveConfigServer } from "@respin/config/app-server";
   14: import { rethrowNextControlFlow } from "../../../../lib/next-control-flow";
   15: import { AccessRefusal } from "../../access-refusal";
   16: import { billingErrorDisplay, billingErrorFromCode } from "../../billing-errors";
   17: import { BillingView, type BillingViewProps, type TierOption } from "./billing-view";
   18: import { STRIPE_REMEDY } from "./copy";
   19: import {
   20:   buyPackAction,
   21:   openPortalAction,
   22:   pauseAction,
   23:   resumeAction,
   24:   setAutoTopupAction,
   25:   subscribeAction,
   26: } from "./actions";
   27: 
   28: const TIER_LABELS: Record<TierOption["tier"], string> = {
   29:   creator: "Creator",
   30:   pro: "Pro",
   31:   studio: "Studio",
   32: };
   33: 
   34: export default async function BillingSettingsPage(props: {
   35:   searchParams: Promise<Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>>;
   36: }) {
   37:   // The real gate, per-page (client-nav caches layouts â€” gate-completeness test).
   38:   // ABOVE the try: `requireUser()` refuses by throwing a `redirect()`.
   39:   const user = await requireUser();
   40:   const search = await props.searchParams;
   41: 
   42:   // Scoping is a REFUSAL PATH (round-2 NOTE): `WorkspaceAccessError` has
   43:   // rendered copy in billing-errors.ts and, until this try existed, no way to
   44:   // reach it from a page.
   45:   let scope: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof respinDb.withWorkspace>>;
   46:   try {
   47:     scope = await respinDb.withWorkspace({ authUserId: user.id });
   48:   } catch (err) {
   49:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
   50:     console.error("[billing] workspace scope unavailable", err);
   51:     return <AccessRefusal copy={billingErrorDisplay(err)} />;
   52:   }
   53:   const errParam = search.e;
   54: 
   55:   const [subscription] = await scope.accessors.subscription();
   56: 
   57:   // ONE liveness definition, four readers. The other three are inside
   58:   // packages/credits (checkout's F1 guard, auto-top-up arming, maybeAutoTopup);
   59:   // this is the fourth, and it is the same function â€” not a page-local idea of
   60:   // what "subscribed" looks like.
   61:   const hasLiveSubscription = subscription
   62:     ? hasLiveStripeSubscription(subscription)
   63:     : false;
   64: 
   65:   let state: BillingViewProps["state"] = { tier: "free", state: "free" };
   66:   let config: BillingViewProps["config"];
   67:   try {
   68:     const active = await getActiveConfigServer();
   69:     const mappedTiers = new Set(Object.values(active.content.stripePriceMap));
   70:     config = {
   71:       ok: true,
   72:       version: active.version,
   73:       tiers: (["creator", "pro", "studio"] as const).map((tier) => ({
   74:         tier,
   75:         label: TIER_LABELS[tier],
   76:         monthlyCredits: active.content.allowances[tier],
   77:         priceMapped: mappedTiers.has(tier),
   78:       })),
   79:       pack: {
   80:         credits: active.content.pack.credits,
   81:         priceUsd: active.content.pack.priceUsd,
   82:         mapped: mappedTiers.has("pack"),
   83:       },
   84:       pauseMonths: active.content.pauseMonths,
   85:     };
   86:   } catch (err) {
   87:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
   88:     console.error("[billing] active config unavailable", err);
   89:     const copy = billingErrorDisplay(err);
   90:     config = { ok: false, title: copy.title, detail: copy.detail };
   91:   }
   92: 
   93:   try {
   94:     const billing = await respinCredits.getBillingState(
   95:       scope.workspaceId,
   96:       new Date()
   97:     );
   98:     state = billing;
   99:   } catch (err) {
  100:     rethrowNextControlFlow(err);
  101:     // getWorkspaceBillingState reads config to resolve a tier, so it fails
  102:     // closed with the config. Say "unknown" rather than defaulting to free â€”
  103:     // the config error box above carries the operator's remedy.
  104:     console.error("[billing] billing state unavailable", err);
  105:     state = { tier: "unknown", state: "unknown" };
  106:   }
  107: 
  108:   return (
  109:     <BillingView
  110:       state={state}
  111:       isOwner={scope.role === "owner"}
  112:       hasLiveSubscription={hasLiveSubscription}
  113:       hasStripeCustomer={Boolean(subscription)}
  114:       autoTopup={{
  115:         enabled: subscription?.autoTopupEnabled ?? false,
  116:         monthlyCapCents: subscription?.autoTopupMonthlyCapCents ?? null,
  117:       }}
  118:       config={config}
  119:       stripe={{ configured: isStripeConfigured(), remedy: STRIPE_REMEDY }}
  120:       error={billingErrorFromCode(
  121:         typeof errParam === "string" ? errParam : undefined
  122:       )}
  123:       showCancel={search.cancel === "1"}
  124:       actions={{
  125:         subscribe: subscribeAction,
  126:         pack: buyPackAction,
  127:         portal: openPortalAction,
  128:         pause: pauseAction,
  129:         resume: resumeAction,
  130:         autoTopup: setAutoTopupAction,
  131:       }}
  132:       cancelHref="/settings/billing?cancel=1"
  133:       usageHref="/usage"
  134:     />
  135:   );
  136: }
===== respin/app/(product)/settings/billing/billing-view.tsx =====
    1: // PURE presentation for /settings/billing (REQ-G01/G03/G08 UI half, REQ-A02).
    2: // The page does the gate, the scoping and the reads; every branch below is
    3: // reachable from a test with a fixture.
    4: //
    5: // THE CANCEL RULE (skill B4, REQ-G08): the cancel flow ALWAYS offers pause
    6: // first. Mechanically, not by arrangement â€” the only control on this page whose
    7: // purpose is cancellation carries `data-cancel="final"`, it exists ONLY inside
    8: // the interstitial, and the interstitial renders the pause offer above it.
    9: // `tests/billing-ui.test.tsx` asserts both halves: no `data-cancel="final"` on
   10: // the ordinary page at all, and on the interstitial the pause offer's marker
   11: // appears earlier in the HTML than it does.
   12: //
   13: // HONESTY NOTE on prices: config carries tier ALLOWANCES and the pack price,
   14: // but tier prices live in Stripe (the setup script creates them; a Stripe price
   15: // amount is immutable). So this page shows the credits a plan includes and
   16: // sends the reader to Stripe for the amount, rather than printing an R-7
   17: // indicative number that could disagree with what the card is actually charged.
   18: import type { ReactNode } from "react";
   19: 
   20: export type FormAction = string | ((formData: FormData) => void | Promise<void>);
   21: 
   22: export type TierOption = {
   23:   tier: "creator" | "pro" | "studio";
   24:   label: string;
   25:   monthlyCredits: number;
   26:   /** False when the active config maps no Stripe price for this tier. */
   27:   priceMapped: boolean;
   28: };

   30: export type BillingViewProps = {
   31:   /**
   32:    * `state: "unknown"` is NOT a fifth billing state â€” it is the honest render
   33:    * when `getWorkspaceBillingState` could not answer (a fail-closed config

   35:    * server could not verify, which is the invented-specifics failure exactly.
   36:    */

   98: function Blocked({ reason }: { reason: string }) {
   99:   return <p style={muted}>{reason}</p>;

  101: 
  102: /**
  103:  * A submit button that is disabled with a NAMED reason, or live. One component
  104:  * so no control on this page can be disabled without saying why â€” the "fail
  105:  * closed, but never without a way forward" rule in button form.
  106:  */
  107: function ActionButton({
  108:   action,
  109:   label,
  110:   blockedBy,
  111:   hidden,
  112:   children,
  113:   testId,
  114:   cancelMarker,
  115: }: {
  116:   action: FormAction;
  117:   label: string;
  118:   blockedBy: string | null;
  119:   hidden?: ReactNode;
  120:   children?: ReactNode;
  121:   testId?: string;
  122:   cancelMarker?: boolean;
  123: }) {
  124:   // The cancel marker rides BOTH branches. Marking only the live form would
  125:   // mean a cancellation control that happens to be disabled (non-owner, no
  126:   // Stripe key) carries no marker â€” and the "no control on the ordinary page
  127:   // reaches cancellation" assertion would pass over it.
  128:   const cancel = cancelMarker ? "final" : undefined;

  133:           {label}
  134:         </button>
  135:         <Blocked reason={blockedBy} />
  136:       </div>
  137:     );
  138:   }
  139:   return (
  140:     <form action={action} data-testid={testId} data-cancel={cancel}>
  141:       {hidden}
  142:       {children}
  143:       <button type="submit">{label}</button>
  144:     </form>
  145:   );
  146: }

  148: export function BillingView(props: BillingViewProps) {

  185:

  192:

  199: 
  200:       <div style={section} data-testid="current-plan">

  202:         <p>

  209:             not map to a plan, so it is being treated as Free rather than
  210:             guessed. An operator can fix it by adding the price id to

  212:             derived at read time.
  213:           </p>
  214:         ) : null}
  215:         {state.state === "grace" && state.graceExpiresAt ? (
  216:           <p data-testid="grace">

  220:           </p>
  221:         ) : null}
  222:         {state.state === "paused" ? (

  224:             Paused â€”{" "}

===== respin/app/(product)/billing-errors.ts =====
    1: // THE ONE PLACE app/** turns a typed package refusal into words on a page.
    2: //
    3: // Why a code map and not `err.message`:
    4: //  - The package messages are written for the person debugging the system, and
    5: //    several of them carry identifiers â€” `LedgerIntegrityError` names ledger
    6: //    row uuids, `ClockSkewError` names two ISO instants. Those belong in the
    7: //    server log, not in a creator's browser (billing/tenancy round-11 NOTE on
    8: //    `customers.ts`, generalised: ids in the log, remedy in the message).
    9: //  - Server actions redirect on failure, so the only channel back to the page
   10: //    is the URL. Putting a MESSAGE there would let anyone hand a creator a link
   11: //    that renders arbitrary text as if the product said it; a code cannot.
   12: //
   13: // The completeness of this map is ASSERTED, not promised: `tests/billing-ui.test.tsx`
   14: // compares HANDLED_ERROR_CLASS_NAMES against every Error subclass exported by
   15: // the two app-facing facades, so a class added to a facade without copy here
   16: // fails the suite instead of degrading to "Something went wrong".
   17: import {
   18:   AlreadySubscribedError,
   19:   AutoTopupCapError,
   20:   BillingRoleError,

  208: export function billingErrorCode(err: unknown): BillingErrorCode {
  209:   for (const h of HANDLERS) {
  210:     if (err instanceof h.cls) return h.code;
  211:   }
  212:   return "unknown";
  213: }
  214: 
  215: export function isBillingErrorCode(
  216:   value: string | undefined | null
  217: ): value is BillingErrorCode {
  218:   return (
  219:     typeof value === "string" &&
  220:     (BILLING_ERROR_CODES as readonly string[]).includes(value)
  221:   );
  222: }

  224: /** Copy for a caught error â€” never the error's own message (see the header). */
  225: export function billingErrorDisplay(err: unknown): BillingErrorCopy & {
  226:   code: BillingErrorCode;
  227: } {
  228:   const code = billingErrorCode(err);
  229:   return { code, ...BILLING_ERROR_COPY[code] };
  230: }
  231: 
  232: /** Copy for a `?e=` code carried back from a server action's redirect. */
  233: export function billingErrorFromCode(
  234:   value: string | undefined | null
  235: ): (BillingErrorCopy & { code: BillingErrorCode }) | null {
  236:   if (value === undefined || value === null || value === "") return null;
  237:   const code: BillingErrorCode = isBillingErrorCode(value) ? value : "unknown";
  238:   return { code, ...BILLING_ERROR_COPY[code] };
  239: }
===== respin/packages/auth/src/server.ts =====
    1: // THE GATE lives here (auth-swap plan, gate-location decision): middleware is
    2: // an optimistic cookie redirect only; every protected page/layout calls
    3: // requireUser()/requireAdmin() â€” client-nav caches layouts, hence per-page.
    4: // The gate-completeness test (respin/tests/gate-completeness.test.ts) enforces
    5: // this mechanically for every page under PROTECTED_PREFIXES.
    6: import { headers } from "next/headers";
    7: import { notFound, redirect } from "next/navigation";
    8: import { toNextJsHandler } from "better-auth/next-js";
    9: import { getServerDb } from "@respin/db";
   10: import { adminAllowed, parseAdminAllowlist } from "./allowlist";
   11: import { createAuth, type Auth } from "./create-auth";
   12: 
   13: let cached: Auth | undefined;
   14: 
   15: /** Lazy runtime instance â€” no env/db access at import time (keyless build). */
   16: export function getAuth(): Auth {
   17:   cached ??= createAuth(getServerDb());
   18:   return cached;
   19: }
   20: 
   21: export type SessionUser = {
   22:   id: string;
   23:   email: string;
   24:   name: string;
   25: };
   26: 
   27: export async function getSessionUser(): Promise<SessionUser | null> {
   28:   const session = await getAuth().api.getSession({
   29:     headers: await headers(),
   30:   });
   31:   if (!session) return null;
   32:   const { id, email, name } = session.user;
   33:   return { id, email, name };
   34: }
   35: 
   36: /** The real /studio gate: no valid session â†’ redirect to sign-in. */
   37: export async function requireUser(): Promise<SessionUser> {
   38:   const user = await getSessionUser();
   39:   if (!user) redirect("/sign-in");
   40:   return user;
   41: }
   42: 
   43: /** The real /admin gate: fail closed â€” empty/unset ADMIN_USER_IDS denies everyone. */
   44: export async function requireAdmin(): Promise<SessionUser> {
   45:   const user = await getSessionUser();
   46:   if (!adminAllowed(user?.id, parseAdminAllowlist(process.env.ADMIN_USER_IDS))) {
   47:     notFound();
   48:   }
   49:   return user as SessionUser;
   50: }
   51:

   53: // (plan-review CHANGE 2). Lazy: nothing constructs at module import, so a
   54: // keyless `next build` importing the route file stays green.
   55: let handlers: ReturnType<typeof toNextJsHandler> | undefined;
   56: function h() {
   57:   handlers ??= toNextJsHandler(getAuth());
   58:   return handlers;
   59: }

   62:   GET: (req: Request) => h().GET(req),
   63:   POST: (req: Request) => h().POST(req),
   64: };
===== respin/packages/auth/src/create-auth.ts =====
    1: import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
    2: import { drizzleAdapter } from "better-auth/adapters/drizzle";
    3: import type { DbLike } from "@respin/db";
    4: 
    5: export type CreateAuthOptions = {
    6:   baseURL?: string;
    7:   secret?: string;
    8: };
    9: 
   10: export function isGoogleConfigured(): boolean {
   11:   return Boolean(
   12:     process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID && process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
   13:   );
   14: }
   15: 
   16: /**
   17:  * The password-reset URL is a BEARER CREDENTIAL (account takeover if leaked).
   18:  * Outside development it must never enter logs â€” and neither does the email
   19:  * (T6: keep PII out of aggregatable logs; the user id suffices for support).
   20:  * Exported for the guard test.
   21:  */
   22: export function resetPasswordLogLine(
   23:   nodeEnv: string | undefined,
   24:   user: { id: string; email: string },
   25:   url: string
   26: ): string {
   27:   if (nodeEnv === "development") {
   28:     return `[dev-only] password reset link for ${user.email}: ${url}`;
   29:   }
   30:   return `password reset requested (user ${user.id})`;
   31: }
   32: 
   33: /**
   34:  * Factory (testability: tests inject a PGlite db and run REAL sign-up flows).
   35:  * The runtime instance is built lazily in server.ts â€” no env read at import.
   36:  */
   37: export function createAuth(db: DbLike, opts: CreateAuthOptions = {}) {
   38:   return betterAuth({
   39:     // The db's schema map already contains the generated auth tables â€”
   40:     // packages/db/src/schema.ts re-exports auth-schema.ts (adapter-wiring pin).
   41:     database: drizzleAdapter(db, { provider: "pg" }),
   42:     secret: opts.secret ?? process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET,
   43:     baseURL: opts.baseURL ?? process.env.BETTER_AUTH_URL,
   44:     emailAndPassword: {
   45:       enabled: true,
   46:       revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset: true,
   47:       // SHORTCUT: no email provider until M6 (digests land there â€” auth-swap
   48:       // plan, Deferral Ledger). Ceiling: users cannot actually receive reset
   49:       // email; dev reads the link from the dev console. Guard: outside
   50:       // development the URL is never logged (resetPasswordLogLine).
   51:       // Upgrade trigger: M6 email provider â€” replace this stub with real send.
   52:       sendResetPassword: async ({ user, url }) => {
   53:         console.log(resetPasswordLogLine(process.env.NODE_ENV, user, url));
   54:       },
   55:     },
   56:     ...(isGoogleConfigured()
   57:       ? {
   58:           socialProviders: {
   59:             google: {
   60:               clientId: process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID as string,
   61:               clientSecret: process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET as string,
   62:             },
   63:           },
   64:         }
   65:       : {}),
   66:   });
   67: }
   68: 
   69: export type Auth = ReturnType<typeof createAuth>;
===== respin/packages/auth/src/allowlist.ts =====
    1: // Admin allowlist (moved here from lib/routes.ts in the auth swap â€” it is
    2: // auth logic, and middleware can no longer check it: Better Auth has no
    3: // stateless edge verification, so the check lives at the server layer).
    4: export function parseAdminAllowlist(raw: string | undefined): Set<string> {
    5:   return new Set(
    6:     (raw ?? "")
    7:       .split(",")
    8:       .map((s) => s.trim())
    9:       .filter(Boolean)
   10:   );
   11: }
   12: 
   13: /**
   14:  * FAIL CLOSED: an unset or empty ADMIN_USER_IDS denies everyone â€”
   15:  * it never admits everyone.
   16:  */
   17: export function adminAllowed(
   18:   userId: string | null | undefined,
   19:   allowlist: Set<string>
   20: ): boolean {
   21:   return (
   22:     typeof userId === "string" && userId.length > 0 && allowlist.has(userId)
   23:   );
   24: }
===== respin/packages/db/src/billing-schema.ts =====
    1: // M1 billing schema (tech-spec Â§2 as amended by R-20 / D-M1-1..8).
    2: // Free tier is the ABSENCE of a subscriptions row (skill B6) â€” never a $0 price.
    3: import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
    4: import {
    5:   boolean,
    6:   check,
    7:   integer,
    8:   jsonb,
    9:   pgEnum,
   10:   pgTable,
   11:   text,
   12:   timestamp,
   13:   uniqueIndex,
   14:   uuid,
   15: } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
   16: import { uuidv7 } from "uuidv7";
   17: import { workspaces } from "./schema";
   18: 
   19: const id = () =>
   20:   uuid("id")
   21:     .primaryKey()
   22:     .$defaultFn(() => uuidv7());
   23: 
   24: // THE COLUMN DEFAULT IS `now()` = `transaction_timestamp()` â€” the instant the
   25: // writing TRANSACTION BEGAN, not the instant of the write (round-10 BLOCK).
   26: // Which tables may keep it, decided once for the whole class rather than per
   27: // column, and audited rather than assumed:
   28: //
   29: //  - `credit_ledger.created_at`: NEVER. It IS the fold order (D-M1-7/D-M1-8), it
   30: //    is compared against `pause_periods.started_at` to compute effective expiry,
   31: //    and it bounds retroactive writes through `latestEventAt`. Every insert in
   32: //    `packages/credits` stamps it explicitly from the clock its guards used, and
   33: //    a source scan (credits/tests/ledger.test.ts) refuses a NEW mint path that
   34: //    quietly takes this default â€” three mint paths were added during Phase 3
   35: //    alone, so "remember to stamp it" is not a control.
   36: //  - `pause_periods.started_at` / `ended_at`: not defaults at all â€” both are
   37: //    caller-supplied, and both callers derive them from `getDbNow`
   38: //    (`clock_timestamp`). `pause_periods.created_at`/`updated_at` ARE defaults
   39: //    and may stay: no derivation reads them (the fold reads started_at/ended_at
   40: //    only â€” checked by grep over packages/**, not assumed).
   41: //  - `stripe_events.received_at`: may stay, and transaction-start is arguably
   42: //    the RIGHT semantic here â€” the D-M1-1 single transaction begins when we
   43: //    start handling the event, so that IS receipt. Nothing reads it, and
   44: //    idempotency is the primary key, never a timestamp. `processed_at` is
   45: //    already stamped from `getDbNow` at the end of the same transaction.
   46: //  - `subscriptions.created_at`/`updated_at`: mirror bookkeeping; no derivation
   47: //    reads either (the order guard uses `mirror_event_at`, which carries
   48: //    Stripe's own `created`).
   49: const createdAt = () =>
   50:   timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow().notNull();
   51: 
   52: const updatedAt = () =>
   53:   timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true })
   54:     .defaultNow()
   55:     .notNull()
   56:     .$onUpdate(() => new Date());
   57: 
   58: // Mutable MIRROR of Stripe state â€” sanctioned non-ledger state (D-M1-6).
   59: // No `tier` column: tier is derived at read time from stripePriceId Ã— the
   60: // active config's stripePriceMap, so a config fix self-heals without replay.
   61: export const subscriptions = pgTable(
   62:   "subscriptions",
   63:   {
   64:     id: id(),
   65:     workspaceId: uuid("workspace_id")
   66:       .notNull()
   67:       .references(() => workspaces.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
   68:     stripeCustomerId: text("stripe_customer_id").notNull(),
   69:     stripeSubscriptionId: text("stripe_subscription_id"),
   70:     stripePriceId: text("stripe_price_id"),
   71:     status: text("status").notNull().default("none"),
   72:     currentPeriodStart: timestamp("current_period_start", {
   73:       withTimezone: true,
   74:     }),
   75:     currentPeriodEnd: timestamp("current_period_end", { withTimezone: true }),
   76:     graceExpiresAt: timestamp("grace_expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
   77:     pausedAt: timestamp("paused_at", { withTimezone: true }),
   78:     resumesAt: timestamp("resumes_at", { withTimezone: true }),
   79:     cancelAtPeriodEnd: boolean("cancel_at_period_end").notNull().default(false),
   80:     // The scheduled end of a subscription that is still LIVE. Both columns
   81:     // exist because Stripe expresses one fact two ways and the evidence run
   82:     // proved the boolean alone is not enough: cancelling through the Customer
   83:     // Portal on api_version 2026-05-27.dahlia emitted
   84:     // `{cancel_at: <ts>, cancel_at_period_end: FALSE, status: active}`, so a
   85:     // mirror reading only the boolean stored "not cancelling" for a
   86:     // subscription Stripe had already scheduled to end, and the billing page
   87:     // told a paying creator nothing. The installed SDK documents `cancel_at`
   88:     // as "a date in the future at which the subscription will automatically
   89:     // get canceled" (stripe@22.5.0 resources/Subscriptions.d.ts:128-130) and
   90:     // the boolean as "will (if status=active) or DID (if status=canceled)
   91:     // cancel at the end of the current billing period" â€” different questions,
   92:     // so both are mirrored and `scheduledCancelAt` (state.ts) is the ONE
   93:     // reader that turns the pair into a date.
   94:     cancelAt: timestamp("cancel_at", { withTimezone: true }),
   95:     autoTopupEnabled: boolean("auto_topup_enabled").notNull().default(false),
   96:     autoTopupMonthlyCapCents: integer("auto_topup_monthly_cap_cents"),
   97:     // Stripe does not guarantee webhook delivery ORDER. This records the
   98:     // `created` timestamp of the newest subscription event already applied to
   99:     // this mirror; a stale event is ignored rather than overwriting newer
  100:     // state (billing code-review CHANGE: order-blind mirror writes).
  101:     mirrorEventAt: timestamp("mirror_event_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  102:     createdAt: createdAt(),
  103:     updatedAt: updatedAt(),
  104:   },
  105:   (t) => [
  106:     uniqueIndex("subscriptions_workspace_uq").on(t.workspaceId),
  107:     uniqueIndex("subscriptions_customer_uq").on(t.stripeCustomerId),
  108:     uniqueIndex("subscriptions_subscription_uq").on(t.stripeSubscriptionId),
  109:   ]
  110: );
  111: 
  112: export const creditKind = pgEnum("credit_kind", [
  113:   "grant",
  114:   "pack",
  115:   "debit",
  116:   "refund",
  117:   "adjust",
  118:   "expiry",
  119: ]);
  120: 
  121: // APPEND-ONLY (non-negotiable 2 / B1): no updatedAt â€” rows are never updated.
  122: // Balance is the D-M1-7 lot-allocation fold; never a stored counter.
  123: export const creditLedger = pgTable(
  124:   "credit_ledger",
  125:   {
  126:     id: id(),
  127:     workspaceId: uuid("workspace_id")
  128:       .notNull()
  129:       .references(() => workspaces.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  130:     delta: integer("delta").notNull(),
  131:     kind: creditKind("kind").notNull(),
  132:     refType: text("ref_type"),
  133:     refId: text("ref_id"),
  134:     reasonCode: text("reason_code"),
  135:     expiresAt: timestamp("expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  136:     // Money attribution for PURCHASED lots (packs, auto-top-ups): feeds the
  137:     // auto-top-up monthly cap (in real cents) and the M6 margin rollup.
  138:     amountCents: integer("amount_cents"),
  139:     // The config version that priced a config-priced row (grants, auto-top-ups).
  140:     configVersion: integer("config_version"),
  141:     stripeEventId: text("stripe_event_id"),
  142:     createdAt: createdAt(),
  143:   },
  144:   (t) => [
  145:     uniqueIndex("credit_ledger_stripe_event_uq").on(t.stripeEventId),
  146:     // D-M1-7 idempotent lazy expiry materialization: one expiry row per lot.
  147:     // Phase-2 handoff pin: an expiry row's ref_id is ALWAYS the consumed lot's
  148:     // ledger uuid (globally unique), which is why this index needs no
  149:     // workspace_id â€” a cross-workspace collision is a writer defect that
  150:     // fails closed here, never a retry.
  151:     uniqueIndex("credit_ledger_expiry_lot_uq")
  152:       .on(t.kind, t.refId)
  153:       .where(sql`${t.kind} = 'expiry'`),
  154:     // ONE pack per Checkout session, whatever the event id (code-review
  155:     // BLOCK). Stripe can drive a session's fulfilment from more than one
  156:     // event â€” `checkout.session.completed` and
  157:     // `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` carry DIFFERENT event ids, so
  158:     // credit_ledger_stripe_event_uq cannot dedupe them and the session minted
  159:     // twice. Stripe's own fulfilment guidance is that a session's handler must
  160:     // be idempotent PER SESSION; the handler pre-checks, and this index is the
  161:     // guarantee under concurrency.
  162:     //
  163:     // Deliberately NOT workspace-keyed, for the same reason as
  164:     // credit_ledger_expiry_lot_uq above: a Stripe Checkout session id is
  165:     // globally unique and belongs to exactly one customer, hence exactly one
  166:     // workspace. Two workspaces claiming one session id is a writer defect (or
  167:     // a forged payload) and must fail closed here rather than mint twice â€” so
  168:     // the global scope IS the guarantee, not an oversight. The handler's
  169:     // pre-check is still workspace-scoped: this index is what holds under
  170:     // concurrency, the pre-check is what makes the ordinary second event
  171:     // converge quietly.
  172:     uniqueIndex("credit_ledger_checkout_session_uq")
  173:       .on(t.refType, t.refId)
  174:       .where(sql`${t.refType} = 'checkout_session'`),
  175:     // ONE monthly allowance per INVOICE, symmetric with the session rule
  176:     // above (code-review CHANGE). Round 3 learned "one mint per business
  177:     // object, not per event id" and applied it to Checkout only; a grant still
  178:     // leaned solely on the event-id unique, so any second event id carrying
  179:     // the same invoice minted a second allowance. Same global-scope reasoning:
  180:     // an invoice id is globally unique and belongs to one customer.
  181:     uniqueIndex("credit_ledger_invoice_grant_uq")
  182:       .on(t.refType, t.refId)
  183:       .where(sql`${t.refType} = 'invoice'`),
  184:     // ONE pack per PAYMENT INTENT â€” the third and last mint path, which had
  185:     // been left leaning on credit_ledger_stripe_event_uq alone while its two
  186:     // siblings above each got a business-object unique (billing review finding
  187:     // 2). Every path that turns a Stripe object into credits now has one, so
  188:     // the rule "one mint per business object, not per event id" is structural
  189:     // for all three rather than for the two that were reported. Same
  190:     // global-scope reasoning as the siblings: a PaymentIntent id is globally
  191:     // unique and belongs to exactly one customer, hence one workspace, so two
  192:     // workspaces claiming one PI is a writer defect that must fail closed here
  193:     // rather than mint twice.
  194:     uniqueIndex("credit_ledger_auto_topup_uq")
  195:       .on(t.refType, t.refId)
  196:       .where(sql`${t.refType} = 'auto_topup'`),
  197:     check("credit_ledger_delta_nonzero", sql`${t.delta} <> 0`),
  198:     check(
  199:       "credit_ledger_delta_sign",
  200:       sql`(${t.kind} IN ('grant','pack','refund') AND ${t.delta} > 0)
  201:           OR (${t.kind} IN ('debit','expiry') AND ${t.delta} < 0)
  202:           OR (${t.kind} = 'adjust')`
  203:     ),
  204:     check(
  205:       "credit_ledger_adjust_reason",
  206:       sql`${t.kind} <> 'adjust' OR ${t.reasonCode} IS NOT NULL`
  207:     ),
  208:     // Review round 1: make the D-M1-7 invariants structural, not prose.
  209:     // An expiry row must name its lot (NULLs would bypass the partial unique).
  210:     check(
  211:       "credit_ledger_expiry_ref",
  212:       sql`${t.kind} <> 'expiry' OR ${t.refId} IS NOT NULL`
  213:     ),
  214:     // grant/pack/refund lots always carry an expiry (nullable only for adjust).
  215:     check(
  216:       "credit_ledger_lot_expiry",
  217:       sql`${t.kind} NOT IN ('grant','pack','refund') OR ${t.expiresAt} IS NOT NULL`
  218:     ),
  219:   ]
  220: );
  221: 
  222: // Webhook idempotency (D-M1-1): written ONLY inside the single-transaction
  223: // dispatch â€” insert + handler + processed-mark commit together, so an existing
  224: // row always means its outcome is final. workspace_id is resolved at receipt
  225: // whenever the customer maps (regardless of outcome) so attributed payloads
  226: // join the REQ-A04 deletion cascade; unattributable rows fall to the M6 sweep.
  227: export const stripeEvents = pgTable(
  228:   "stripe_events",
  229:   {
  230:     id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  231:     type: text("type").notNull(),
  232:     payload: jsonb("payload").notNull(),
  233:     workspaceId: uuid("workspace_id").references(() => workspaces.id, {
  234:       onDelete: "cascade",
  235:     }),
  236:     stripeCustomerId: text("stripe_customer_id"),
  237:     outcome: text("outcome").notNull(),
  238:     receivedAt: timestamp("received_at", { withTimezone: true })
  239:       .defaultNow()
  240:       .notNull(),
  241:     processedAt: timestamp("processed_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  242:   },
  243:   (t) => [
  244:     // The Phase-3 handoff vocabulary, made structural (review round 1).
  245:     check(
  246:       "stripe_events_outcome",
  247:       sql`${t.outcome} IN ('processed','refused_unknown_customer','refused_identity_mismatch','ignored')`
  248:     ),
  249:   ]
  250: );
  251: 
  252: // Append-only versioned runtime config (D-M1-2 / B5): active = max(version).
  253: export const configVersions = pgTable("config_versions", {
  254:   version: integer("version").primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(),
  255:   content: jsonb("content").notNull(),
  256:   createdBy: text("created_by").notNull(),
  257:   createdAt: createdAt(),
  258: });
  259: 
  260: // One row per pause period (D-M1-3). NOT append-only: closing the open row by
  261: // setting ended_at on resume is its ONE sanctioned update; no other column is
  262: // ever rewritten. Expiry-clock suspension is derivation-time (D-M1-7 fold).
  263: export const pausePeriods = pgTable(
  264:   "pause_periods",
  265:   {
  266:     id: id(),
  267:     workspaceId: uuid("workspace_id")
  268:       .notNull()
  269:       .references(() => workspaces.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  270:     startedAt: timestamp("started_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
  271:     endedAt: timestamp("ended_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  272:     // The KNOWLEDGE time of the OPEN, symmetric with ended_known_at below
  273:     // (round-3 CHANGE 1). Migration 0007 fixed one side of the bound and left
  274:     // the other on the wrong clock: `ensurePauseEnded` compared the caller's
  275:     // knowledge time (`event.created`) against `started_at`, which is our
  276:     // PROCESSING time. Probe-reproduced through the real migrations â€” a pause
  277:     // Stripe applied at T0 but processed at T0+5min, then resumed in Stripe at
  278:     // T0+2min, saw 3 minutes of "staleness" and returned false: the pause row
  279:     // stays OPEN, `effectiveExpiry` freezes every lot's clock indefinitely,
  280:     // `state.ts` reports `paused` and M3's debit would refuse with
  281:     // WorkspacePausedError â€” while Stripe bills normally and no further event
  282:     // is coming. It self-heals only if the owner presses Resume in-app.
  283:     //
  284:     // Nullable for the same reason as ended_known_at: rows written before this
  285:     // column existed have none, and both readers fall back to the processing
  286:     // column there (the old, conservative behaviour).
  287:     startedKnownAt: timestamp("started_known_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  288:     // The KNOWLEDGE time of the close, as distinct from the moment we wrote it.
  289:     //
  290:     // `ended_at` is the DB clock at PROCESSING time. For the owner's own resume
  291:     // that is the same instant as the knowledge; for a webhook it is not â€” a
  292:     // resume event delivered after Stripe backoff is processed minutes after
  293:     // `event.created`. ensurePauseStarted's staleness bound compares a caller's
  294:     // `knownAt` against the last close, so mixing the two clocks made it refuse
  295:     // a REAL, current pause: resume at T0 processed at T0+5m, portal pause at
  296:     // T0+2m, bound sees 3m of "staleness" and writes no pause_periods row at
  297:     // all â€” expiry clocks keep running through a pause Stripe has applied, and
  298:     // no further event is coming (round-2 NOTE 3).
  299:     //
  300:     // Nullable: rows written before this column existed have none, and the
  301:     // bound falls back to `ended_at` there (the old, conservative behaviour).
  302:     endedKnownAt: timestamp("ended_known_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  303:     createdAt: createdAt(),
  304:     updatedAt: updatedAt(),
  305:   },
  306:   (t) => [
  307:     uniqueIndex("pause_periods_open_uq")
  308:       .on(t.workspaceId)
  309:       .where(sql`${t.endedAt} IS NULL`),
  310:     // The one sanctioned update must be unable to record a nonsense interval â€”
  311:     // a negative pause would shift expiries BACKWARD in the D-M1-7 fold.
  312:     check(
  313:       "pause_periods_interval",
  314:       sql`${t.endedAt} IS NULL OR ${t.endedAt} > ${t.startedAt}`
  315:     ),
  316:     // The knowledge of a close cannot exist without the close (round-3 NOTE).
  317:     // Both are written in ONE `.set()` by recordPauseEnd, so this is structural
  318:     // rather than aspirational â€” it makes a future writer that stamps only the
  319:     // knowledge column impossible.
  320:     //
  321:     // DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and this is the interesting half: there is NO check
  322:     // ordering the two knowledge columns against each other, and there must not
  323:     // be. `ensurePauseEnded` tolerates CLOCK_SKEW_MS, so a legitimate close can
  324:     // carry `ended_known_at` up to 60s BEFORE `started_known_at` (Stripe's
  325:     // `event.created` is second-granularity while the pause row is written on
  326:     // the millisecond DB clock). A `ended_known_at > started_known_at` check
  327:     // would therefore reject real resumes on the money path â€” the same class of
  328:     // defect migration 0007 and 0008 exist to fix. Nor is there one relating a
  329:     // knowledge column to its processing column: knowledge legitimately
  330:     // PRECEDES processing (that is the whole point), and by no bounded amount,
  331:     // since Stripe's redelivery backoff is unbounded.
  332:     check(
  333:       "pause_periods_ended_known",
  334:       sql`${t.endedKnownAt} IS NULL OR ${t.endedAt} IS NOT NULL`
  335:     ),
  336:   ]
  337: );

===== respin/packages/credits/src/ledger.ts =====
    1: // Ledger operations â€” the SOLE writers of credit_ledger (Phase 3 lint fences
    2: // this package as the only importer of these tables outside packages/db).
    3: // Every op is TxLike-composable (B3: M3's generation pipeline composes
    4: // debitCredits into the same transaction that persists the generation).
    5: //
    6: // THE WRITE CLOCK (round-10 BLOCK, and the other half of round 7's read-clock
    7: // fix). Every insert below stamps `created_at` EXPLICITLY; none of them may
    8: // take the column default. The default is `now()` = `transaction_timestamp()`,
    9: // fixed when the transaction BEGAN â€” up to a whole lock-wait earlier than the
   10: // state the write was validated against. Round 7 moved the fold's `asOf` to
   11: // `clock_timestamp()` and left this behind, and the two clocks disagreeing is
   12: // not a cosmetic drift:
   13: //
   14: //   A debit transaction BEGINs at t0 and blocks on `takeWorkspaceLock`. An
   15: //   `invoice.paid` grant commits at t1 > t0. The debit acquires the lock at t2,
   16: //   folds at t2, SEES the grant, and is correctly allowed â€” and then writes its
   17: //   row at `created_at = t0`. Every later fold sorts that debit BEFORE the
   18: //   grant that funded it, finds no live lot, and throws
   19: //   `LedgerIntegrityError: â€¦ over-consumes` â€” PERMANENTLY, because the ledger
   20: //   is append-only and the row cannot be removed. `deriveBalance` then throws
   21: //   forever for that workspace: no usage page, no debit, no refund, while
   22: //   webhook grants keep landing and the customer keeps paying.
   23: //
   24: // The rule, stated once for the whole class rather than per call site:
   25: //
   26: //  - ALLOCATING writes (debit, negative adjust) stamp the fold's OWN `asOf` â€”
   27: //    the exact instant their balance was validated at. Every row that fold saw
   28: //    is <= it by construction, so the row can never sort before a lot it
   29: //    consumed. (Expiry rows materialized by that same fold carry the same
   30: //    instant and a smaller uuidv7, so they replay first â€” which is the order
   31: //    the remainder they recorded was computed in.)
   32: //  - LOT writes (grant, pack, positive adjust, refund) stamp a
   33: //    `clock_timestamp()` read taken in the same statement sequence. They do not
   34: //    allocate, so an early stamp could not over-consume â€” but `effectiveExpiry`
   35: //    compares a lot's `created_at` against `pause_periods.started_at`, which IS
   36: //    the DB clock, so a transaction-start stamp could make a lot look BORN
   37: //    BEFORE a pause it did not exist for and inflate its expiry (the
   38: //    pre-creation inflation class the tenancy round-1 BLOCK closed).
   39: //    `latestEventAt` reads the same column to bound retroactive writes. One
   40: //    rule beats an exception list nobody re-derives.
   41: //
   42: // `tests/ledger.test.ts` pins BOTH halves: a behavioural case that sleeps
   43: // inside a transaction and asserts every writer's row postdates
   44: // `transaction_timestamp()`, and a source scan asserting every
   45: // `.insert(creditLedger)` in `src/**` sets `createdAt` â€” so a NEW mint path
   46: // cannot quietly rejoin the default.

  140: export async function adjustCredits(
  141:   tx: TxLike,
  142:   p: AdjustParams
  143: ): Promise<CreditLedgerRow> {
  144:   if (!Number.isInteger(p.delta) || p.delta === 0) {
  145:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError("adjust delta must be a non-zero integer");
  146:   }
  147:   // See the write-clock note at the top of this file: an allocating adjust is
  148:   // dated at the instant its balance was validated, a lot-producing one at the
  149:   // instant it is written. Never the transaction's start.
  150:   let createdAt: Date;
  151:   if (p.delta < 0) {
  152:     // Negative adjust allocates like a debit: same clock + pause + balance guards.
  153:     const at = p.at;
  154:     if (!at) {
  155:       throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  156:         "negative adjust requires an explicit `at` (it allocates like a debit)"
  157:       );
  158:     }

  160:     await assertWriteClock(tx, p.workspaceId, at);
  161:     if (await hasOpenPause(tx, p.workspaceId)) {
  162:       throw new WorkspacePausedError();
  163:     }
  164:     const view = await deriveBalanceInTx(tx, p.workspaceId);
  165:     if (view.balance < -p.delta) {
  166:       throw new InsufficientCreditsError(view.balance, -p.delta);
  167:     }
  168:     createdAt = view.asOf;
  169:   } else {
  170:     createdAt = await getDbNow(tx);
  171:   }
  172:   const [row] = await tx
  173:     .insert(creditLedger)
  174:     .values({
  175:       workspaceId: p.workspaceId,
  176:       delta: p.delta,
  177:       kind: "adjust",
  178:       reasonCode: p.reasonCode,
  179:       expiresAt: p.delta > 0 ? (p.expiresAt ?? null) : null,
  180:       refType: p.refType,
  181:       refId: p.refId,
  182:       createdAt,
  183:     })
  184:     .returning();
  185:   return row;
  186: }

  204: /**
  205:  * Refund against a specific debit. expires_at is computed per D-M1-7: the
  206:  * latest effective expiry of the lots the original debit consumed â€” a refund
  207:  * of expiring credits must not mint never-expiring ones; a refund of a debit
  208:  * whose lots have since expired is born expired (fail-safe, stated policy).
  209:  * NO M1 caller â€” ships package-tested for the M6 admin surface.
  210:  */
  211: export async function refundCredits(
  212:   tx: TxLike,
  213:   p: RefundParams
  214: ): Promise<CreditLedgerRow> {
  215:   assertPositiveInt(p.amount, "refund amount");
  216:   await takeWorkspaceLock(tx, p.workspaceId);
  217:   const view = await deriveBalanceInTx(tx, p.workspaceId);
  218:   // Rebuild the allocation trace from the authoritative fold.
  219:   const rows = await tx
  220:     .select()
  221:     .from(creditLedger)
  222:     .where(eq(creditLedger.workspaceId, p.workspaceId))
  223:     .orderBy(asc(creditLedger.createdAt), asc(creditLedger.id));
  224:   const pauses = await tx
  225:     .select()
  226:     .from(pausePeriods)
  227:     .where(eq(pausePeriods.workspaceId, p.workspaceId))
  228:     .orderBy(asc(pausePeriods.startedAt));
  229:   const fold = foldLedger(rows, pauses, view.asOf);
  230: 
  231:   const debit = rows.find((r) => r.id === p.originalDebitId);
  232:   if (!debit || debit.kind !== "debit") {
  233:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  234:       `refundCredits: ${p.originalDebitId} is not a debit row of this workspace`
  235:     );
  236:   }
  237:   const alreadyRefunded = rows
  238:     .filter((r) => r.kind === "refund" && r.refId === p.originalDebitId)
  239:     .reduce((s, r) => s + r.delta, 0);
  240:   if (p.amount + alreadyRefunded > -debit.delta) {
  241:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  242:       `refundCredits: refunding ${p.amount} would exceed the original debit (${-debit.delta}, already refunded ${alreadyRefunded})`
  243:     );
  244:   }
  245:   const trace = fold.allocations.get(p.originalDebitId) ?? [];
  246:   const lotById = new Map(fold.lots.map((l) => [l.id, l]));
  247:   const expiries = trace
  248:     .map((t) => lotById.get(t.lotId)?.effectiveExpiresAt ?? null)
  249:     .filter((d): d is Date => d !== null);
  250:   const sourceFrozen = trace.some(
  251:     (t) => lotById.get(t.lotId)?.frozen === true
  252:   );
  253:   const sourceNever = trace.some((t) => {
  254:     const lot = lotById.get(t.lotId);
  255:     return lot ? lot.effectiveExpiresAt === null && !lot.frozen : false;
  256:   });
  257:   let expiresAt: Date;
  258:   if (expiries.length > 0) {
  259:     expiresAt = new Date(Math.max(...expiries.map((d) => d.getTime())));
  260:   } else if (sourceFrozen) {
  261:     // Distinct from never-expiring (billing round-1 note): the source lot's
  262:     // clock is frozen by an OPEN pause â€” refund after resume instead.
  263:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  264:       "refundCredits: the consumed lots' expiry clocks are frozen by an open pause â€” resume the subscription first, then refund"
  265:     );
  266:   } else if (sourceNever) {
  267:     throw new RefundSourceNeverExpiresError();
  268:   } else {
  269:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  270:       `refundCredits: no allocation trace found for debit ${p.originalDebitId}`
  271:     );
  272:   }
  273: 
  274:   const [row] = await tx
  275:     .insert(creditLedger)
  276:     .values({
  277:       workspaceId: p.workspaceId,
  278:       delta: p.amount,
  279:       kind: "refund",
  280:       expiresAt,
  281:       refType: "debit",
  282:       refId: p.originalDebitId,
  283:       stripeEventId: p.stripeEventId,
  284:       // A refund is a LOT, and `view.asOf` is the instant this transaction read
  285:       // the ledger it is refunding against â€” no later row can exist for this
  286:       // workspace (the advisory lock is held), so the two clock rules agree here.
  287:       createdAt: view.asOf,
  288:     })
  289:     .returning();
  290:   return row;
  291: }
