===== respin/packages/credits/src/fold.ts =====
    1: // The D-M1-7 chronological lot-allocation fold â€” PURE (no I/O), so the
    2: // table-driven suite can drive it with fixed dates. Semantics (R-20):
    3: // - grant/pack/refund and positive adjust rows are consumable LOTS;
    4: // - debit and negative adjust ALLOCATE against live lots in D-M1-8 order
    5: //   (soonest effective expiry first; equal â†’ older first; then grants before
    6: //   packs; never-expiring lots last);
    7: // - expiry rows are REPLAYED as history, never recomputed;
    8: // - pause periods suspend expiry clocks: effective expiry = expires_at shifted
    9: //   by the chronological pause-overlap fold; an open pause freezes the clock.
   10: import type { CreditLedgerRow, PausePeriod } from "@respin/db";
   11: 
   12: export class LedgerIntegrityError extends Error {
   13:   constructor(message: string) {
   14:     super(message);
   15:     this.name = "LedgerIntegrityError";
   16:   }
   17: }
   18: 
   19: export type LotView = {
   20:   id: string;
   21:   kind: CreditLedgerRow["kind"];
   22:   createdAt: Date;
   23:   /** Stored expiry (null = never-expiring adjust lot). */
   24:   expiresAt: Date | null;
   25:   /** Pause-shifted expiry; null = never expires; Infinity â‡’ frozen by an open pause (represented as null too, with frozen=true). */
   26:   effectiveExpiresAt: Date | null;
   27:   frozen: boolean;
   28:   initial: number;
   29:   remaining: number;
   30:   /** True when an expiry row already materialized this lot's remainder. */
   31:   expiredByRow: boolean;
   32: };
   33: 
   34: export type FoldResult = {
   35:   balance: number;
   36:   lots: LotView[];
   37:   /** Lots whose remainder should be materialized as expiry rows (vs asOf). */
   38:   expiryCandidates: { lotId: string; remaining: number }[];
   39:   /** Allocation trace: debit/negative-adjust row id â†’ consumed lot portions. */
   40:   allocations: Map<string, { lotId: string; amount: number }[]>;
   41: };
   42: 
   43: const KIND_RANK: Record<string, number> = {
   44:   grant: 0,
   45:   pack: 1,
   46:   refund: 2,
   47:   adjust: 3,
   48: };
   49: 
   50: /**
   51:  * Pause-shifted effective expiry. Chronological fold per D-M1-3/D-M1-7 â€”
   52:  * counting ONLY the pause time that overlaps the lot's own lifetime
   53:  * [lotCreatedAt, shifted expiry): a clock that wasn't running yet cannot be
   54:  * suspended, so a pause that ended before the lot existed shifts nothing and
   55:  * a pause straddling the lot's creation counts only its post-creation portion
   56:  * (tenancy code-review BLOCK 2).
   57:  */
   58: export function effectiveExpiry(
   59:   expiresAt: Date | null,
   60:   pauses: PausePeriod[],
   61:   lotCreatedAt: Date
   62: ): { at: Date | null; frozen: boolean } {
   63:   if (expiresAt === null) return { at: null, frozen: false };
   64:   let eff = expiresAt.getTime();
   65:   const born = lotCreatedAt.getTime();
   66:   // Merge overlapping periods first (billing round-2 NOTE): the writer refuses
   67:   // a second open pause, but a â‰¤60s-skew overlap between adjacent periods
   68:   // would otherwise double-count the shared seconds.
   69:   const sorted = mergePauses(pauses);
   70:   for (const p of sorted) {
   71:     const overlapStart = Math.max(p.startedAt.getTime(), born);
   72:     if (overlapStart >= eff) continue; // no overlap with the lot's clock
   73:     if (p.endedAt === null) {
   74:       // Open pause overlapping the lot's lifetime before its (shifted)
   75:       // expiry: the clock is frozen â€” the lot cannot expire while paused.
   76:       return { at: null, frozen: true };
   77:     }
   78:     if (p.endedAt.getTime() <= born) continue; // ended before the lot existed
   79:     eff += p.endedAt.getTime() - overlapStart;
   80:   }
   81:   return { at: new Date(eff), frozen: false };
   82: }
   83: 
   84: /** Coalesce overlapping/touching pause intervals (open pause swallows the tail). */
   85: function mergePauses(pauses: PausePeriod[]): PausePeriod[] {
   86:   const sorted = [...pauses].sort(
   87:     (a, b) => a.startedAt.getTime() - b.startedAt.getTime()
   88:   );
   89:   const merged: PausePeriod[] = [];
   90:   for (const p of sorted) {
   91:     const last = merged[merged.length - 1];
   92:     if (
   93:       last &&
   94:       (last.endedAt === null ||
   95:         last.endedAt.getTime() >= p.startedAt.getTime())
   96:     ) {
   97:       if (last.endedAt !== null) {
   98:         const end =
   99:           p.endedAt === null
  100:             ? null
  101:             : new Date(Math.max(last.endedAt.getTime(), p.endedAt.getTime()));
  102:         merged[merged.length - 1] = { ...last, endedAt: end };
  103:       }
  104:       // last is open: it already swallows p entirely.
  105:       continue;
  106:     }
  107:     merged.push(p);
  108:   }
  109:   return merged;
  110: }
  111: 
  112: function isLive(lot: LotView, t: Date): boolean {
  113:   if (lot.remaining <= 0 || lot.expiredByRow) return false;
  114:   if (lot.effectiveExpiresAt === null) return true; // never / frozen
  115:   return lot.effectiveExpiresAt.getTime() > t.getTime();
  116: }
  117: 
  118: function allocationOrder(a: LotView, b: LotView): number {
  119:   const aNever = a.effectiveExpiresAt === null;
  120:   const bNever = b.effectiveExpiresAt === null;
  121:   if (aNever !== bNever) return aNever ? 1 : -1; // never-expiring last
  122:   if (!aNever && !bNever) {
  123:     const d =
  124:       (a.effectiveExpiresAt as Date).getTime() -
  125:       (b.effectiveExpiresAt as Date).getTime();
  126:     if (d !== 0) return d; // soonest effective expiry first
  127:   }
  128:   const c = a.createdAt.getTime() - b.createdAt.getTime();
  129:   if (c !== 0) return c; // older first
  130:   return (KIND_RANK[a.kind] ?? 9) - (KIND_RANK[b.kind] ?? 9); // grants before packs
  131: }
  132: 
  133: /** True for rows the fold treats as consumable lots (D-M1-7's six kinds). */
  134: function isLotRow(r: CreditLedgerRow): boolean {
  135:   return (
  136:     r.kind === "grant" ||
  137:     r.kind === "pack" ||
  138:     r.kind === "refund" ||
  139:     (r.kind === "adjust" && r.delta > 0)
  140:   );
  141: }
  142: 
  143: /**
  144:  * Replay rank for rows sharing a `created_at` to the microsecond
  145:  * (billing round-11 NOTE, `fold.ts:145-148`). The write-clock rule
  146:  * (ledger.ts) makes ties REAL, not hypothetical: expiry rows materialized by a
  147:  * fold and the debit stamped with that same fold's `asOf` carry the identical
  148:  * instant by construction. Until now the tie-break was `id.localeCompare`, i.e.
  149:  * uuidv7 order â€” true today because one process inserts the expiry rows first,
  150:  * and an assumption the moment a second backend writes in the same microsecond
  151:  * with a skewed clock. That assumption is worth removing because the failure is
  152:  * PERMANENT: replaying a debit before the lot that funded it throws
  153:  * `over-consumes`, and replaying it before its own expiry row throws
  154:  * `materialization drifted`, on a table that can never be edited to fix it.
  155:  *
  156:  * The order is the causal one, and it is the order the writers already intend:
  157:  *   0 lots (a lot must exist before anything allocates against it)
  158:  *   1 expiry (materialization claims a lot's remainder as the fold measured it)
  159:  *   2 allocating rows (debit / negative adjust)
  160:  * `id` remains the final tie-break, so ordering stays total and deterministic.
  161:  */
  162: function replayRank(r: CreditLedgerRow): number {
  163:   if (isLotRow(r)) return 0;
  164:   if (r.kind === "expiry") return 1;
  165:   return 2;
  166: }
  167: 
  168: /**
  169:  * Replay the ledger up to `asOf` (events with createdAt <= asOf) against the
  170:  * pause history. Deterministic; throws LedgerIntegrityError on history the
  171:  * schema CHECKs should have made impossible.
  172:  */
  173: export function foldLedger(
  174:   rows: CreditLedgerRow[],
  175:   pauses: PausePeriod[],
  176:   asOf: Date
  177: ): FoldResult {
  178:   const events = rows
  179:     .filter((r) => r.createdAt.getTime() <= asOf.getTime())
  180:     .sort(
  181:       (a, b) =>
  182:         a.createdAt.getTime() - b.createdAt.getTime() ||
  183:         replayRank(a) - replayRank(b) ||
  184:         a.id.localeCompare(b.id)
  185:     );
  186: 
  187:   const lots = new Map<string, LotView>();
  188:   const allocations: FoldResult["allocations"] = new Map();
  189: 
  190:   for (const ev of events) {
  191:     if (isLotRow(ev)) {
  192:       const eff = effectiveExpiry(ev.expiresAt, pauses, ev.createdAt);
  193:       lots.set(ev.id, {
  194:         id: ev.id,
  195:         kind: ev.kind,
  196:         createdAt: ev.createdAt,
  197:         expiresAt: ev.expiresAt,
  198:         effectiveExpiresAt: eff.at,
  199:         frozen: eff.frozen,
  200:         initial: ev.delta,
  201:         remaining: ev.delta,
  202:         expiredByRow: false,
  203:       });
  204:       continue;
  205:     }
  206:     if (ev.kind === "expiry") {
  207:       if (!ev.refId) {
  208:         throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  209:           `expiry row ${ev.id} names no lot (schema CHECK should forbid this)`
  210:         );
  211:       }
  212:       const lot = lots.get(ev.refId);
  213:       if (!lot) {
  214:         throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  215:           `expiry row ${ev.id} references unknown lot ${ev.refId}`
  216:         );
  217:       }
  218:       if (-ev.delta !== lot.remaining) {
  219:         throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  220:           `expiry row ${ev.id} expires ${-ev.delta} but lot ${lot.id} has ${lot.remaining} remaining â€” materialization drifted`
  221:         );
  222:       }
  223:       lot.remaining = 0;
  224:       lot.expiredByRow = true;
  225:       continue;
  226:     }
  227:     // debit, or negative adjust: allocate per D-M1-8.
  228:     const amount = -ev.delta;
  229:     if (amount <= 0) {
  230:       throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  231:         `row ${ev.id} kind ${ev.kind} has non-negative delta ${ev.delta} in the allocating branch`
  232:       );
  233:     }
  234:     const live = [...lots.values()]
  235:       .filter((l) => isLive(l, ev.createdAt))
  236:       .sort(allocationOrder);
  237:     let toConsume = amount;
  238:     const trace: { lotId: string; amount: number }[] = [];
  239:     for (const lot of live) {
  240:       if (toConsume === 0) break;
  241:       const take = Math.min(lot.remaining, toConsume);
  242:       lot.remaining -= take;
  243:       toConsume -= take;
  244:       trace.push({ lotId: lot.id, amount: take });
  245:     }
  246:     if (toConsume > 0) {
  247:       throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  248:         `row ${ev.id} over-consumes: ${toConsume} of ${amount} could not be allocated â€” a debit was written past the available balance`
  249:       );
  250:     }
  251:     allocations.set(ev.id, trace);
  252:   }
  253: 
  254:   const lotViews = [...lots.values()];
  255:   const balance = lotViews
  256:     .filter((l) => isLive(l, asOf))
  257:     .reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.remaining, 0);
  258:   const expiryCandidates = lotViews
  259:     .filter(
  260:       (l) =>
  261:         l.remaining > 0 &&
  262:         !l.expiredByRow &&
  263:         !l.frozen &&
  264:         l.effectiveExpiresAt !== null &&
  265:         l.effectiveExpiresAt.getTime() <= asOf.getTime()
  266:     )
  267:     .map((l) => ({ lotId: l.id, remaining: l.remaining }));
  268: 
  269:   return { balance, lots: lotViews, expiryCandidates, allocations };
  270: }
===== respin/packages/credits/src/balance.ts =====
    1: // The SOLE balance authority (B1, D-M1-7). Balance is the fold's answer;
    2: // lazy expiry materialization keeps sum(delta) of ALL rows literally equal to
    3: // it. Lock composition: given a caller tx (debit path â€” lock already held) the
    4: // materialization JOINS that tx; given a bare db it opens its own tx under the
    5: // per-workspace advisory lock (usage-page path).
    6: import { asc, eq } from "drizzle-orm";
    7: import type { DbLike, TxLike, VerifiedWorkspaceId } from "@respin/db";
    8: import { creditLedger, pausePeriods } from "@respin/db";
    9: import { foldLedger, type FoldResult, type LotView } from "./fold";
   10: import { getDbNow, takeWorkspaceLock } from "./clock";
   11: 
   12: export type BalanceView = {
   13:   balance: number;
   14:   lots: LotView[];
   15:   asOf: Date;
   16: };
   17: 
   18: async function loadHistory(tx: TxLike, workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId) {
   19:   const rows = await tx
   20:     .select()
   21:     .from(creditLedger)
   22:     .where(eq(creditLedger.workspaceId, workspaceId))
   23:     .orderBy(asc(creditLedger.createdAt), asc(creditLedger.id));
   24:   const pauses = await tx
   25:     .select()
   26:     .from(pausePeriods)
   27:     .where(eq(pausePeriods.workspaceId, workspaceId))
   28:     .orderBy(asc(pausePeriods.startedAt));
   29:   return { rows, pauses };
   30: }
   31: 
   32: /**
   33:  * Fold + lazy materialization inside an EXISTING transaction that already
   34:  * holds (or now takes â€” same-session re-acquire is a no-op) the workspace
   35:  * advisory lock. Writes are keyed to DB now(); `at` shapes the returned view
   36:  * only (a historical `at` is a pure read).
   37:  */
   38: export async function deriveBalanceInTx(
   39:   tx: TxLike,
   40:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   41:   at?: Date
   42: ): Promise<BalanceView> {
   43:   await takeWorkspaceLock(tx, workspaceId);
   44:   const dbNow = await getDbNow(tx);
   45: 
   46:   let { rows, pauses } = await loadHistory(tx, workspaceId);
   47:   let fold = foldLedger(rows, pauses, dbNow);
   48: 
   49:   if (fold.expiryCandidates.length > 0) {
   50:     // Materialize each crossed lot's remainder (idempotent per lot via the
   51:     // partial unique; on-conflict-do-nothing then re-read per D-M1-7).
   52:     //
   53:     // `createdAt: dbNow` â€” never the column default (round-10 BLOCK; the write-
   54:     // clock rule is stated in full at the top of ledger.ts). An expiry row is an
   55:     // ALLOCATING row: it claims a lot's whole remainder as computed by THIS
   56:     // fold. Stamped at `transaction_timestamp()` it would replay earlier than
   57:     // the instant that remainder was measured â€” before debits this same
   58:     // transaction is about to write, and before rows committed while we waited
   59:     // for the lock â€” and `foldLedger` throws `materialization drifted` (or
   60:     // over-consumes) on a ledger that can never be edited to fix it. Stamping
   61:     // the fold's own `asOf` also keeps the row visible to the re-read below,
   62:     // which filters on `createdAt <= dbNow`.
   63:     await tx
   64:       .insert(creditLedger)
   65:       .values(
   66:         fold.expiryCandidates.map((c) => ({
   67:           workspaceId,
   68:           delta: -c.remaining,
   69:           kind: "expiry" as const,
   70:           refType: "lot",
   71:           refId: c.lotId,
   72:           createdAt: dbNow,
   73:         }))
   74:       )
   75:       .onConflictDoNothing();
   76:     ({ rows, pauses } = await loadHistory(tx, workspaceId));
   77:     fold = foldLedger(rows, pauses, dbNow);
   78:   }
   79: 
   80:   const viewAt = at && at.getTime() < dbNow.getTime() ? at : dbNow;
   81:   const view: FoldResult =
   82:     viewAt === dbNow ? fold : foldLedger(rows, pauses, viewAt);
   83:   return { balance: view.balance, lots: view.lots, asOf: viewAt };
   84: }
   85: 
   86: /** Bare-db entry (usage page): opens its own locked transaction. */
   87: export async function deriveBalance(
   88:   db: DbLike,
   89:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   90:   at?: Date
   91: ): Promise<BalanceView> {
   92:   return db.transaction((tx) => deriveBalanceInTx(tx, workspaceId, at));
   93: }
===== respin/packages/credits/src/state.ts =====
    1: // Tier/state machine (D-M1-4 lazy grace). Tier is derived AT READ TIME from
    2: // subscriptions.stripePriceId Ã— the active config's stripePriceMap â€” a config
    3: // fix self-heals without event replay; an unmapped price fails closed to free
    4: // entitlements with a named reason the UI can turn into a remedy.
    5: import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
    6: import type { DbLike, TxLike, VerifiedWorkspaceId } from "@respin/db";
    7: import { subscriptions } from "@respin/db";
    8: import { getActiveConfig, type SubscriptionTier } from "@respin/config";
    9: 
   10: const ACTIVE_STATUSES = new Set(["active", "trialing"]);
   11: 
   12: /**
   13:  * The statuses a Stripe subscription can never come back from. Everything else
   14:  * â€” including `unpaid` and `incomplete`, which a customer can still pay out of
   15:  * â€” leaves a subscription that EXISTS in Stripe and will keep emitting events.
   16:  */
   17: export const IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES = new Set(["canceled", "incomplete_expired"]);
   18: 
   19: /**
   20:  * "Does a Stripe subscription exist for this workspace right now?" â€” the ONE
   21:  * definition, because two readers of one mirror row disagreeing is how both
   22:  * round-6 gate findings happened (billing round-6 BLOCK + CHANGE):
   23:  *
   24:  *  - `actions.ts` used to answer this with a LIVE_STATUSES allowlist that also
   25:  *    counted `cancelAtPeriodEnd` as liveness. Nothing ever resets that flag, so
   26:  *    after the ordinary REQ-G01 self-serve "cancel at period end" the mirror
   27:  *    read {canceled, cancelAtPeriodEnd: true} â€” free everywhere else, but
   28:  *    "already subscribed" here, refusing the owner a re-subscribe FOREVER and
   29:  *    pointing them at a Customer Portal with nothing left to manage.
   30:  *  - The same allowlist omitted `unpaid`, so the F1 double-billing guard waved
   31:  *    a second Checkout through for a subscription that is still alive in
   32:  *    Stripe â€” the two-subscriptions-one-workspace end state the single-row
   33:  *    mirror cannot even represent.
   34:  *
   35:  * Both disappear when liveness is derived from irreversibility rather than
   36:  * from a hand-maintained list: a subscription is live iff we have its id and
   37:  * its last known status is not one of the two it cannot return from.
   38:  */
   39: export function hasLiveStripeSubscription(row: {
   40:   stripeSubscriptionId: string | null;
   41:   status: string;
   42: }): boolean {
   43:   return (
   44:     row.stripeSubscriptionId !== null && !IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(row.status)
   45:   );
   46: }
   47: 
   48: /**
   49:  * When is this subscription scheduled to END? â€” the ONE reader of the pair of
   50:  * columns Stripe uses for one fact, for the same reason `hasLiveStripeSubscription`
   51:  * is the one reader of liveness: two callers answering it differently is how
   52:  * both round-6 findings happened.
   53:  *
   54:  * The evidence run (2026-08-17) cancelled through the Customer Portal on
   55:  * api_version 2026-05-27.dahlia and the payload carried `cancel_at: <ts>` with
   56:  * `cancel_at_period_end: FALSE` and `status: active`. A mirror reading only the
   57:  * boolean therefore stored "not cancelling" for a subscription Stripe had
   58:  * already scheduled to end, and the billing page told a paying creator nothing.
   59:  * The installed SDK documents them as different questions â€” `cancel_at` is "a
   60:  * date in the future at which the subscription will automatically get canceled",
   61:  * the boolean is "will (if status=active) or DID (if status=canceled) cancel at
   62:  * the end of the current billing period" (stripe@22.5.0
   63:  * resources/Subscriptions.d.ts:128-134) â€” so both are mirrored and read here:
   64:  *
   65:  *  - an explicit `cancelAt` wins, because it is the date Stripe will act on;
   66:  *  - the legacy boolean still resolves to the period end, so a subscription
   67:  *    cancelled through the older shape (or an older API version) is not lost;
   68:  *  - a DEAD subscription is never "scheduled to end" â€” it already has, and
   69:  *    DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS clears both columns anyway; keying on liveness
   70:  *    means a stale value cannot outlive the subscription even if it did.
   71:  */
   72: export function scheduledCancelAt(row: {
   73:   stripeSubscriptionId: string | null;
   74:   status: string;
   75:   cancelAt: Date | null;
   76:   cancelAtPeriodEnd: boolean;
   77:   currentPeriodEnd: Date | null;
   78: }): Date | null {
   79:   if (!hasLiveStripeSubscription(row)) return null;
   80:   if (row.cancelAt) return row.cancelAt;
   81:   return row.cancelAtPeriodEnd ? row.currentPeriodEnd : null;
   82: }
   83: 
   84: export type BillingState = {
   85:   tier: SubscriptionTier | "free";
   86:   state: "free" | "active" | "grace" | "paused";
   87:   reason?: "unmapped_price";
   88:   graceExpiresAt?: Date;
   89:   resumesAt?: Date;
   90:   /** Set when the subscription is live but scheduled to end (REQ-G01). */
   91:   cancelAt?: Date;
   92: };
   93: 
   94: export async function getWorkspaceBillingState(
   95:   db: DbLike | TxLike,
   96:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   97:   at: Date
   98: ): Promise<BillingState> {
   99:   const [sub] = await db
  100:     .select()
  101:     .from(subscriptions)
  102:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  103:     .limit(1);
  104:   // Free = ABSENCE of a subscriptions row (B6) â€” or a dead one.
  105:   if (!sub) return { tier: "free", state: "free" };
  106: 
  107:   const resolveTier = async (): Promise<
  108:     { tier: SubscriptionTier; reason?: undefined } | { tier: "free"; reason: "unmapped_price" }
  109:   > => {
  110:     if (!sub.stripePriceId) return { tier: "free", reason: "unmapped_price" };
  111:     const { content } = await getActiveConfig(db);
  112:     const mapped = content.stripePriceMap[sub.stripePriceId];
  113:     if (mapped === "creator" || mapped === "pro" || mapped === "studio") {
  114:       return { tier: mapped };
  115:     }
  116:     return { tier: "free", reason: "unmapped_price" };
  117:   };
  118: 
  119:   // One computation, shared by every LIVE state below (active / paused /
  120:   // grace): a scheduled end is a fact about the subscription, not about which
  121:   // of those three it is in.
  122:   const endsAt = scheduledCancelAt(sub) ?? undefined;
  123: 
  124:   if (sub.pausedAt !== null) {
  125:     const t = await resolveTier();
  126:     return {
  127:       tier: t.tier,
  128:       state: "paused",
  129:       reason: t.reason,
  130:       resumesAt: sub.resumesAt ?? undefined,
  131:       cancelAt: endsAt,
  132:     };
  133:   }
  134:   if (ACTIVE_STATUSES.has(sub.status)) {
  135:     const t = await resolveTier();
  136:     return { tier: t.tier, state: "active", reason: t.reason, cancelAt: endsAt };
  137:   }
  138:   if (sub.status === "past_due") {
  139:     if (sub.graceExpiresAt && sub.graceExpiresAt.getTime() > at.getTime()) {
  140:       const t = await resolveTier();
  141:       return {
  142:         tier: t.tier,
  143:         state: "grace",
  144:         reason: t.reason,
  145:         graceExpiresAt: sub.graceExpiresAt,
  146:         cancelAt: endsAt,
  147:       };
  148:     }
  149:     return { tier: "free", state: "free" };
  150:   }
  151:   // canceled / none / incomplete / anything else â†’ free.
  152:   return { tier: "free", state: "free" };
  153: }
===== respin/packages/credits/src/pause.ts =====
    1: // Pause record-keeping (D-M1-3, REQ-G08). recordPauseStart/End are
    2: // record-keepers only â€” the pauseMonths bounds check lives in Phase 3's
    3: // pauseSubscription action, which resolves months against config BEFORE
    4: // calling Stripe and this. Closing the open row (ended_at) is pause_periods'
    5: // ONE sanctioned update; the schema CHECK enforces ended_at > started_at.
    6: //
    7: // DUAL-TRUTH WARNING (Phase 3 contract): pause truth lives in pause_periods
    8: // (debit guard) AND the subscriptions.pausedAt mirror (billing state) â€” they
    9: // stay in sync ONLY because these two functions write both in one tx. Phase 3
   10: // must NEVER write subscriptions.pausedAt directly; always go through here.
   11: //
   12: // TWO CLOCKS, FOUR COLUMNS (round-3 CHANGE 1 â€” read this before touching a
   13: // bound). Every pause bound in this file compares a caller's KNOWLEDGE time
   14: // (`event.created` for a webhook; "now" for the owner's own action) against a
   15: // stored bound. `started_at`/`ended_at` are PROCESSING times â€” the DB clock at
   16: // the moment we wrote the row, which for a webhook delivered after Stripe's
   17: // backoff can be minutes later. `started_known_at`/`ended_known_at` are the
   18: // knowledge times. A bound that mixes the two is a live money defect in both
   19: // directions, and both directions have now happened:
   20: //   - the OPEN side (migration 0007): a late-processed resume made a real,
   21: //     current pause look stale, so no pause row was written at all;
   22: //   - the CLOSE side (migration 0008): a late-processed PAUSE made a real,
   23: //     current resume look stale, so the pause stayed OPEN forever â€” frozen
   24: //     expiry clocks, `state: "paused"`, and M3's debit refusing, while Stripe
   25: //     bills normally and no further event is coming.
   26: // Knowledge is compared with knowledge on BOTH sides now, with the
   27: // `?? <processing column>` fallback keeping pre-migration rows conservative.
   28: import { and, desc, eq, isNotNull, isNull, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
   29: import type { PausePeriod, TxLike, VerifiedWorkspaceId } from "@respin/db";
   30: import { pausePeriods, subscriptions } from "@respin/db";
   31: import { assertWriteClock, CLOCK_SKEW_MS } from "./clock";
   32: import { LedgerIntegrityError } from "./fold";
   33: 
   34: export async function hasOpenPause(
   35:   tx: TxLike,
   36:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId
   37: ): Promise<boolean> {
   38:   const [open] = await tx
   39:     .select({ id: pausePeriods.id })
   40:     .from(pausePeriods)
   41:     .where(
   42:       and(
   43:         eq(pausePeriods.workspaceId, workspaceId),
   44:         isNull(pausePeriods.endedAt)
   45:       )
   46:     )
   47:     .limit(1);
   48:   return open !== undefined;
   49: }
   50: 
   51: /**
   52:  * @param knownAt the moment the CALLER knew about this pause â€” `event.created`
   53:  * for a webhook, omitted (then `at`) for the owner's own action. Stored as
   54:  * `started_known_at` so the CLOSE-side staleness bound compares knowledge with
   55:  * knowledge rather than with our processing time (round-3 CHANGE 1).
   56:  */
   57: export async function recordPauseStart(
   58:   tx: TxLike,
   59:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   60:   at: Date,
   61:   resumesAt?: Date,
   62:   knownAt?: Date
   63: ): Promise<PausePeriod> {
   64:   await assertWriteClock(tx, workspaceId, at);
   65:   if (await hasOpenPause(tx, workspaceId)) {
   66:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
   67:       "recordPauseStart: an open pause already exists for this workspace"
   68:     );
   69:   }
   70:   const [row] = await tx
   71:     .insert(pausePeriods)
   72:     .values({ workspaceId, startedAt: at, startedKnownAt: knownAt ?? at })
   73:     .returning();
   74:   await tx
   75:     .update(subscriptions)
   76:     .set({ pausedAt: at, resumesAt: resumesAt ?? null })
   77:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
   78:   return row;
   79: }
   80: 
   81: /**
   82:  * CONVERGENT pause record-keepers (code-review CHANGE). A pause is committed
   83:  * locally by TWO writers â€” the owner's pauseSubscription action and the
   84:  * reconciling customer.subscription.updated webhook â€” in either order. These
   85:  * converge (returning whether they changed anything) instead of throwing, so
   86:  * whichever writer loses the race never surfaces a failure for an operation
   87:  * Stripe has already performed.
   88:  *
   89:  * The strict recordPauseStart/recordPauseEnd keep their throwing contract for
   90:  * callers that genuinely mean "this must be a state change".
   91:  *
   92:  * A true concurrent interleaving (both see no open pause, both insert) is
   93:  * still caught by pause_periods_open_uq; that 23505 is NOT an idempotency
   94:  * constraint, so it propagates and Stripe redelivers â€” it never becomes a
   95:  * silent 200.
   96:  */
   97: /**
   98:  * @param knownAt OPTIONAL staleness bound, SYMMETRIC with ensurePauseEnded's
   99:  * (billing round-10 NOTE 3). Round 8 bounded the CLOSE side and left the OPEN
  100:  * side unbounded, which leaves this live:
  101:  *
  102:  *   the owner pauses; the reconciling `customer.subscription.updated` (created
  103:  *   during the pause, carrying `pause_collection`) is delayed; the owner then
  104:  *   RESUMES, and `resumeSubscription` deliberately does not stamp
  105:  *   `mirrorEventAt` (that watermark means "a full subscription snapshot", and
  106:  *   stamping it from a partial write is a regression this handler has already
  107:  *   made once); the delayed snapshot sails through the order guard and
  108:  *   RE-OPENS the pause. Credits frozen and `state = "paused"` for a paying
  109:  *   customer, plus a permanent spurious `pause_periods` row that shifts every
  110:  *   lot's effective expiry through the D-M1-7 fold â€” and no further event is
  111:  *   coming, because Stripe has already told us everything it knows.
  112:  *
  113:  * A pause period that ENDED after the moment the caller is reporting on cannot
  114:  * be one the caller knows about, so its snapshot must not start a new one. Same
  115:  * CLOCK_SKEW_MS tolerance and the same reason as the close side: Stripe's
  116:  * `event.created` is second-granularity while `ended_at` is the millisecond DB
  117:  * clock, so the ordinary pause-then-reconcile is routinely a few hundred ms
  118:  * "older" than the row it reconciles. Omitted (the owner's own pause action)
  119:  * means "now" â€” no bound.
  120:  *
  121:  * `knownAt` is also RECORDED (as `started_known_at`), because it is what a
  122:  * later ensurePauseEnded compares itself against â€” round-3 CHANGE 1.
  123:  */
  124: export async function ensurePauseStarted(
  125:   tx: TxLike,
  126:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
  127:   at: Date,
  128:   resumesAt?: Date,
  129:   knownAt?: Date
  130: ): Promise<boolean> {
  131:   // THE STALENESS TEST RUNS FIRST â€” before the already-open early return
  132:   // (billing round-11 NOTE, `pause.ts:104-119`). It used to sit below it, so
  133:   // the bound protected only the "open a pause" branch while the `resumesAt`
  134:   // write below ran UNBOUNDED. That leaves this live: pause 1 (resumes in
  135:   // March) â†’ owner resumes â†’ owner pauses again (pause 2, resumes in June) â†’
  136:   // the delayed pause-1-era snapshot lands, sees an open pause, and rewrites
  137:   // the mirror's `resumesAt` to MARCH â€” a date belonging to a pause that ended,
  138:   // on a pause that has not. No further event is coming to correct it. It is
  139:   // display-only today (`state.ts` reads `resumesAt` into `BillingState`; the
  140:   // expiry fold reads `pause_periods`, never this column) â€” and Phase 4 is what
  141:   // displays it, on both the usage page's frozen notice and the settings page.
  142:   //
  143:   // A caller whose knowledge predates a resume we have already recorded knows
  144:   // nothing about the pause that is open now, so it may neither start one nor
  145:   // restate its resume date.
  146:   if (knownAt) {
  147:     const lastClose = await lastPauseCloseKnownAt(tx, workspaceId);
  148:     if (lastClose && lastClose.getTime() - knownAt.getTime() > CLOCK_SKEW_MS) {
  149:       return false;
  150:     }
  151:   }
  152:   if (await hasOpenPause(tx, workspaceId)) {
  153:     // Already paused â€” converge on the FACT of the pause, but never let the
  154:     // resume DATE drift (code-review CHANGE): a re-pause of a different
  155:     // length gives Stripe a new resumes_at, and if the mirror keeps the old
  156:     // one the owner is shown a date that will never happen. Before the
  157:     // convergence change the strict recordPauseStart threw here, so this
  158:     // information could not be silently lost; converging without this update
  159:     // would have made losing it the normal path.
  160:     if (resumesAt) {
  161:       await tx
  162:         .update(subscriptions)
  163:         .set({ resumesAt })
  164:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
  165:     }
  166:     return false;
  167:   }
  168:   await recordPauseStart(tx, workspaceId, at, resumesAt, knownAt);
  169:   return true;
  170: }
  171: 
  172: /**
  173:  * Converge the MIRROR on "not paused" when no pause period is open.
  174:  *
  175:  * The owner's resume path could reach a state where the two truths disagreed â€”
  176:  * `subscriptions.pausedAt` set, no open `pause_periods` row (a reconciling
  177:  * webhook closed the period without touching the mirror, or a pause was ever
  178:  * recorded only in the mirror). `ensurePauseEnded` returns false there, and
  179:  * `resumeSubscription` then redirected with no error at all: the Resume button
  180:  * appeared to do nothing while the page kept saying "Paused", with no event
  181:  * coming to correct it (round-2 NOTE 4).
  182:  *
  183:  * It lives HERE, beside the other two writers, because of this file's own
  184:  * dual-truth rule: nothing outside pause.ts writes `subscriptions.pausedAt`.
  185:  * It is deliberately NOT called from `ensurePauseEnded` â€” that helper's `false`
  186:  * also means "this snapshot is too stale to be believed", and clearing the
  187:  * mirror on THAT branch would undo a pause the owner just opened.
  188:  */
  189: export async function clearPauseMirror(
  190:   tx: TxLike,
  191:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId
  192: ): Promise<boolean> {
  193:   if (await hasOpenPause(tx, workspaceId)) return false;
  194:   const rows = await tx
  195:     .update(subscriptions)
  196:     .set({ pausedAt: null, resumesAt: null })
  197:     .where(
  198:       and(
  199:         eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId),
  200:         isNotNull(subscriptions.pausedAt)
  201:       )
  202:     )
  203:     .returning({ id: subscriptions.id });
  204:   return rows.length > 0;
  205: }
  206: 
  207: /**
  208:  * The KNOWLEDGE time of the most recent close (the open-side bound's left half).
  209:  *
  210:  * Ordered AND projected on `coalesce(ended_known_at, ended_at)` â€” one
  211:  * expression, so "most recent" and "what is returned" cannot disagree
  212:  * (round-3 NOTE). Ordering on `ended_at` while returning `ended_known_at` was
  213:  * safe only via the separate argument that pause periods cannot overlap; that
  214:  * reasoning step is now removed rather than re-verified.
  215:  *
  216:  * The fallback covers rows written before `ended_known_at` existed, where the
  217:  * processing time is the only close time we have (the old, conservative
  218:  * behaviour).
  219:  */
  220: async function lastPauseCloseKnownAt(
  221:   tx: TxLike,
  222:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId
  223: ): Promise<Date | null> {
  224:   const closeKnownAt = sql<Date>`coalesce(${pausePeriods.endedKnownAt}, ${pausePeriods.endedAt})`;
  225:   const [row] = await tx
  226:     .select({ knownAt: closeKnownAt })
  227:     .from(pausePeriods)
  228:     .where(
  229:       and(
  230:         eq(pausePeriods.workspaceId, workspaceId),
  231:         isNotNull(pausePeriods.endedAt)
  232:       )
  233:     )
  234:     .orderBy(desc(closeKnownAt))
  235:     .limit(1);
  236:   if (!row?.knownAt) return null;
  237:   return row.knownAt instanceof Date ? row.knownAt : new Date(row.knownAt);
  238: }
  239: 
  240: /**
  241:  * @param knownAt OPTIONAL staleness bound for callers whose knowledge has a
  242:  * timestamp â€” the webhook's `event.created` (billing round-7 NOTE). A pause
  243:  * that STARTED after the moment the caller is reporting on cannot be one the
  244:  * caller knows about, so it must not be closed by it: the owner's
  245:  * `pauseSubscription` writes the local pause without stamping `mirrorEventAt`
  246:  * (that watermark means "a full subscription snapshot", and stamping it from a
  247:  * partial write is a regression this handler has already made once), so a
  248:  * `customer.subscription.updated` older than the pause but newer than the last
  249:  * snapshot sails through the order guard and would close a pause opened
  250:  * seconds ago. Omitted (the owner's own resume action) means "now" â€” no bound.
  251:  *
  252:  * The left half of the comparison is the pause's KNOWLEDGE time
  253:  * (`started_known_at`, falling back to `started_at` for pre-0008 rows), NOT its
  254:  * processing time. Migration 0007 fixed the open side and left this one mixing
  255:  * clocks, which round 3 reproduced in PGlite through the real migrations: a
  256:  * pause Stripe applied at T0 but processed at T0+5min, then resumed in Stripe
  257:  * at T0+2min, saw 3 minutes of "staleness" and returned false â€” the pause row
  258:  * stays OPEN, `effectiveExpiry` freezes every lot's clock indefinitely, and
  259:  * NO FURTHER EVENT IS COMING. It self-heals only if the owner presses Resume
  260:  * in-app.
  261:  *
  262:  * The comparison carries the package's existing CLOCK_SKEW_MS tolerance, and
  263:  * must: Stripe's `event.created` is SECOND-granularity while `started_known_at`
  264:  * is second-granularity for webhooks and the millisecond DB clock for the
  265:  * owner's own pause, so the reconciling snapshot for a pause Stripe has just
  266:  * applied is routinely a few hundred ms "older" than the row it is
  267:  * reconciling. Without the tolerance this guard would refuse the ordinary
  268:  * resume. It bites where it should: a snapshot created MINUTES before the
  269:  * pause was known about.
  270:  */
  271: export async function ensurePauseEnded(
  272:   tx: TxLike,
  273:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
  274:   at: Date,
  275:   knownAt?: Date
  276: ): Promise<boolean> {
  277:   const open = await openPause(tx, workspaceId);
  278:   if (!open) return false;
  279:   const openKnownAt = open.startedKnownAt ?? open.startedAt;
  280:   if (knownAt && openKnownAt.getTime() - knownAt.getTime() > CLOCK_SKEW_MS) {
  281:     return false;
  282:   }
  283:   // `knownAt` is RECORDED, not only checked: it is what a later
  284:   // ensurePauseStarted compares itself against, and `at` (processing time) is
  285:   // not the same clock (round-2 NOTE 3).
  286:   await recordPauseEnd(tx, workspaceId, at, knownAt);
  287:   return true;
  288: }
  289: 
  290: /** The workspace's open pause row, if any (the one shape both helpers need). */
  291: async function openPause(
  292:   tx: TxLike,
  293:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId
  294: ): Promise<PausePeriod | undefined> {
  295:   const [open] = await tx
  296:     .select()
  297:     .from(pausePeriods)
  298:     .where(
  299:       and(
  300:         eq(pausePeriods.workspaceId, workspaceId),
  301:         isNull(pausePeriods.endedAt)
  302:       )
  303:     )
  304:     .limit(1);
  305:   return open;
  306: }
  307: 
  308: /**
  309:  * @param knownAt the moment the CALLER knew about this resume â€” `event.created`
  310:  * for a webhook, omitted (then `at`) for the owner's own action. Stored as
  311:  * `ended_known_at` so the open-side staleness bound compares knowledge with
  312:  * knowledge rather than with our processing time.
  313:  */
  314: export async function recordPauseEnd(
  315:   tx: TxLike,
  316:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
  317:   at: Date,
  318:   knownAt?: Date
  319: ): Promise<PausePeriod> {
  320:   await assertWriteClock(tx, workspaceId, at);
  321:   const [open] = await tx
  322:     .select()
  323:     .from(pausePeriods)
  324:     .where(
  325:       and(
  326:         eq(pausePeriods.workspaceId, workspaceId),
  327:         isNull(pausePeriods.endedAt)
  328:       )
  329:     )
  330:     .limit(1);
  331:   if (!open) {
  332:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  333:       "recordPauseEnd: no open pause exists for this workspace"
  334:     );
  335:   }
  336:   if (at.getTime() <= open.startedAt.getTime()) {
  337:     throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  338:       `recordPauseEnd: at (${at.toISOString()}) must be after the pause start (${open.startedAt.toISOString()})`
  339:     );
  340:   }
  341:   const [closed] = await tx
  342:     .update(pausePeriods)
  343:     .set({ endedAt: at, endedKnownAt: knownAt ?? at })
  344:     .where(eq(pausePeriods.id, open.id))
  345:     .returning();
  346:   await tx
  347:     .update(subscriptions)
  348:     .set({ pausedAt: null, resumesAt: null })
  349:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
  350:   return closed;
  351: }

   37:    * A subscription in this status can only have metadata and default_source

   46:         : "This workspace already has a live subscription â€” a second Checkout would create a second Stripe subscription (double-billing). Manage or change the plan in the Customer Portal instead."

  155: // Delegated to the ONE definition in state.ts (round-6 gate: this file's own

  179: export async function createTierCheckoutUrl(
  180:   db: DbLike,
  181:   scope: WorkspaceScope,
  182:   tier: "creator" | "pro" | "studio",
  183:   email: string,
  184:   urls: CheckoutUrls
  185: ): Promise<string> {
  186:   assertOwner(scope);
  187:   const existing = await subscriptionRow(db, scope);
  188:   if (existing && isLive(existing)) throw new AlreadySubscribedError(existing.status);
  189:   const { content } = await getActiveConfig(db);
  190:   const priceId = Object.entries(content.stripePriceMap).find(
  191:     ([, t]) => t === tier
  192:   )?.[0];
  193:   if (!priceId) throw new UnknownTierPriceError(tier);
  194:   const customer = await getOrCreateCustomer(db, scope.workspaceId, email);
  195:   // The F1 guard above reads the MIRROR, and the mirror only moves when the
  196:   // webhook lands â€” so between "customer finishes Checkout" and "webhook
  197:   // arrives" the guard reads `none` and waves a second Checkout through.
  198:   // That window is seconds wide on the happy path and unbounded when Stripe
  199:   // is retrying, and two completed Checkouts are two Stripe subscriptions on
  200:   // one workspace: the customer is billed twice, and the mirror (single-row,
  201:   // by workspace) can only ever remember one of them, so the second bills on
  202:   // forever with nothing in our database pointing at it. The plain
  203:   // double-click and the two-tab race land in the same window
  204:   // (billing review finding 3).
  205:   //
  206:   // A durable lock would need a column, a release path, and a stale-lock
  207:   // sweeper â€” three new failure modes guarding a race that Stripe already
  208:   // solves: an idempotency key makes the SECOND create return the FIRST
  209:   // session instead of a new one. Concurrent callers compute the same key
  210:   // (every input is durable state both of them read), so at most one
  211:   // Checkout Session â€” hence at most one subscription â€” can exist per
  212:   // (workspace, price, subscription-generation). The user simply gets their
  213:   // existing Checkout page back, which is also the better outcome than an
  214:   // error telling them to try again.
  215:   //
  216:   // `stripeSubscriptionId` is the generation counter: it is null before the
  217:   // first subscription and holds the DEAD id after a cancellation, so the
  218:   // subscribe â†’ cancel â†’ re-subscribe flow computes a different key and gets
  219:   // a fresh session rather than a replay of the completed one.
  220:   //
  221:   // EVERY input is durable database state â€” deliberately NOT the tier and NOT
  222:   // the URLs (billing round-5 CHANGE, both directions found by the gate).
  223:   // Including the tier scoped the guarantee per-price, so two racers choosing
  224:   // DIFFERENT tiers got different keys, two sessions and two subscriptions â€”
  225:   // the one end state the single-row mirror cannot even represent. Including a
  226:   // hash of the caller's URLs made the guarantee depend on an argument this
  227:   // package cannot control: a future caller putting a nonce in `successUrl`
  228:   // would have switched it off silently. Keyed on workspace and generation
  229:   // alone, the invariant is exact and self-contained: AT MOST ONE Checkout
  230:   // Session per workspace per subscription generation, whatever the caller
  231:   // varies. A variation now produces a LOUD typed refusal below instead.
  232:   //
  233:   // Stated consequence, in exchange: an owner who opens a Creator checkout and
  234:   // then picks Pro before finishing gets CheckoutInFlightError until the first
  235:   // session lapses, rather than a second session. That is the same refusal F1
  236:   // makes once the subscription exists, moved earlier to the only window where
  237:   // double billing was still reachable.
  238:   //
  239:   // Second stated consequence: Stripe drops idempotency keys after 24h and
  240:   // Checkout Sessions expire after 24h from the same instant, so near that
  241:   // boundary a replay can hand back the URL of a just-expired session. The
  242:   // user sees Stripe's own "session expired" page and the next attempt (past
  243:   // the key's TTL) creates a fresh one â€” self-correcting, and never a charge.
  244:   const idempotencyKey = `checkout:${scope.workspaceId}:${existing?.stripeSubscriptionId ?? "none"}`;
  245:   const session = await getStripe()
  246:     .checkout.sessions.create(
  247:       {
  248:         mode: "subscription",
  249:         customer,
  250:         line_items: [{ price: priceId, quantity: 1 }],
  251:         success_url: urls.successUrl,
  252:         cancel_url: urls.cancelUrl,
  253:         metadata: { workspace_id: scope.workspaceId },
  254:       },
  255:       { idempotencyKey }
  256:     )
  257:     .catch((err: unknown) => {
  258:       // Stripe refuses a key replayed with different parameters. Reaching
  259:       // here means a checkout for this workspace is already open on different
  260:       // terms â€” surface that as the typed, explained refusal it is, rather
  261:       // than letting a raw Stripe 400 reach an owner clicking Subscribe.
  262:       if ((err as { type?: string })?.type === "StripeIdempotencyError") {
  263:         throw new CheckoutInFlightError(tier);
  264:       }
  265:       throw err;
  266:     });
  267:   if (!session.url) throw new StripeSessionUrlMissingError("tier");
  268:   return session.url;
  269: }

  315: /** Pause 1â€“N months (bounds from config `pauseMonths`, REQ-G08/R-12). */
  316: export async function pauseSubscription(
  317:   db: DbLike,
  318:   scope: WorkspaceScope,
  319:   months: number,
  320:   at: Date
  321: ): Promise<void> {
  322:   assertOwner(scope);
  323:   const { content } = await getActiveConfig(db);
  324:   if (
  325:     !Number.isInteger(months) ||
  326:     months < content.pauseMonths.min ||
  327:     months > content.pauseMonths.max
  328:   ) {
  329:     throw new PauseLengthError(
  330:       months,
  331:       content.pauseMonths.min,
  332:       content.pauseMonths.max
  333:     );
  334:   }
  335:   const sub = await liveSubscription(db, scope);
  336:   if (!sub?.stripeSubscriptionId) {
  337:     throw new NoLiveSubscriptionError("pause a subscription");
  338:   }
  339:   // Clamped, not overflowed: a pause started on 31 January used to resume on
  340:   // 3 March, i.e. longer than the `pauseMonths.max` the check above enforces
  341:   // (billing review finding 4 â€” see months.ts).
  342:   const resumesAt = addMonthsUtc(at, months);
  343:   // Stripe first; local records only after the API succeeded. If the local
  344:   // write then fails, the customer.subscription.updated webhook reconciles
  345:   // (its pause-sync branch), so the two truths converge.
  346:   await getStripe().subscriptions.update(sub.stripeSubscriptionId, {
  347:     pause_collection: {
  348:       behavior: "void",
  349:       resumes_at: Math.floor(resumesAt.getTime() / 1000),
  350:     },
  351:   });
  352:   await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
  353:     const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  354:     // CONVERGE, never throw (code-review CHANGE): Stripe has already paused
  355:     // the subscription, and its reconciling customer.subscription.updated may
  356:     // have landed first. Without this the loser of that race shows the owner a
  357:     // failure for an operation that DID happen. Both writers now share ONE
  358:     // convergent form (pause.ts), so they cannot drift apart again.
  359:     await ensurePauseStarted(tx, scope.workspaceId, now, resumesAt);
  360:   });
  361: }
  362: 
  363: export async function resumeSubscription(
  364:   db: DbLike,
  365:   scope: WorkspaceScope
  366: ): Promise<void> {
  367:   assertOwner(scope);
  368:   const [sub] = await db
  369:     .select()
  370:     .from(subscriptions)
  371:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, scope.workspaceId))
  372:     .limit(1);
  373:   if (!sub?.stripeSubscriptionId || sub.pausedAt === null) {
  374:     throw new NotPausedError();
  375:   }
  376:   await getStripe().subscriptions.update(sub.stripeSubscriptionId, {
  377:     pause_collection: "",
  378:   });
  379:   await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
  380:     const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  381:     // Same convergence as pause: "no open pause" is exactly the state the
  382:     // reconciling webhook leaves behind when it wins the race, and that must
  383:     // not be an error for the owner (code-review CHANGE).
  384:     const closed = await ensurePauseEnded(tx, scope.workspaceId, now);
  385:     if (!closed) {
  386:       // ...but converging on the PERIOD is not converging on the MIRROR, and
  387:       // `state.ts` reads the mirror. With `pausedAt` set and no open period (a
  388:       // reconciling webhook closed the period without the mirror, or a pause
  389:       // that only ever reached the mirror) this returned silently: the Resume
  390:       // button appeared to do nothing, the page still said "Paused", and no
  391:       // event was coming to correct it (round-2 NOTE 4). Stripe has already
  392:       // been un-paused by the call above, so clearing is the truthful state â€”
  393:       // and it goes through pause.ts, the only module allowed to write
  394:       // `subscriptions.pausedAt`.
  395:       await clearPauseMirror(tx, scope.workspaceId);
  396:     }
  397:   });
  398: }

  400: /** Auto-top-up opt-in + monthly cap: mirror config, not Stripe state. */
  401: export async function setAutoTopup(
  402:   db: DbLike,
  403:   scope: WorkspaceScope,
  404:   opts: { enabled: boolean; monthlyCapCents?: number }
  405: ): Promise<void> {
  406:   assertOwner(scope);
  407:   if (opts.enabled) {
  408:     if (
  409:       opts.monthlyCapCents === undefined ||
  410:       !Number.isInteger(opts.monthlyCapCents) ||
  411:       opts.monthlyCapCents <= 0
  412:     ) {
  413:       throw new AutoTopupCapError();
  414:     }
  415:   }
  416:   const [row] = await db
  417:     .select()
  418:     .from(subscriptions)
  419:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, scope.workspaceId))
  420:     .limit(1);
  421:   if (!row) throw new NoStripeCustomerError("Auto-top-up");
  422:   // ARMING the flag requires a LIVE subscription, through the ONE definition
  423:   // (billing round-10 CHANGE 4). The only check here used to be "a subscriptions
  424:   // row exists", so a canceled or never-subscribed workspace could still reach
  425:   // {status: canceled, autoTopupEnabled: true} â€” precisely the state
  426:   // DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS was introduced to make impossible, and precisely
  427:   // what `maybeAutoTopup`'s own liveness guard refuses to act on. The trigger
  428:   // refusing is NOT enough: Phase 4's billing UI is the next reader of this row
  429:   // and would show auto-top-up as ON for a workspace that can never be charged,
  430:   // which is the tail wagging the dog. One definition, three readers (here,
  431:   // maybeAutoTopup, and the F1 guard via liveSubscription).
  432:   //
  433:   // DISABLING is deliberately NOT guarded: it can only move the row toward the
  434:   // safe state, and refusing it would trap an owner whose subscription died
  435:   // while the flag was armed with a switch they cannot turn off.
  436:   if (opts.enabled && !isLive(row)) {
  437:     throw new NoLiveSubscriptionError("arm auto-top-up");
  438:   }
  439:   await db
  440:     .update(subscriptions)
  441:     .set({
  442:       autoTopupEnabled: opts.enabled,
  443:       autoTopupMonthlyCapCents: opts.enabled ? opts.monthlyCapCents : null,
  444:     })
  445:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, scope.workspaceId));
  446: }
===== respin/packages/credits/src/stripe/auto-topup.ts =====
    1: // Request-time auto-top-up trigger (D-M1-4; REQ-G03). Purchases EXACTLY ONE
    2: // standard pack per trigger (plan-review F4; if one pack doesn't cover the
    3: // shortfall the debit still refuses and the user buys manually). M1 ships and
    4: // tests this function directly; NO M1 code calls it â€” the debit-refusal call
    5: // site is M3's generation pipeline (master-plan Deferral Ledger).
    6: import { and, eq, gte, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
    7: import {
    8:   creditLedger,
    9:   subscriptions,
   10:   type DbLike,
   11:   type VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   12: } from "@respin/db";
   13: import { getActiveConfig } from "@respin/config";
   14: import { hasLiveStripeSubscription } from "../state";
   15: import { getStripe } from "./adapter";
   16: 
   17: export type AutoTopupResult =
   18:   | { triggered: true; paymentIntentId: string }
   19:   | {
   20:       triggered: false;
   21:       reason:
   22:         | "disabled"
   23:         | "paused"
   24:         | "cap_reached"
   25:         | "no_customer"
   26:         | "not_subscribed";
   27:     };
   28: 
   29: /**
   30:  * @param shortfall credits the refused debit was short by â€” the Phase-3
   31:  * handoff contract's third argument, restored here (billing review finding 7:
   32:  * the plan pins `maybeAutoTopup(db, workspaceId, shortfall, at)` and the code
   33:  * had drifted to a 3-arg form, so M3's debit-refusal call site â€” the only
   34:  * caller there will ever be, and one nobody has written yet â€” would have been
   35:  * coded against a signature that does not exist).
   36:  *
   37:  * It is VALIDATED, not scaled on: plan-review F4 decided one standard pack per
   38:  * trigger, so a shortfall larger than `pack.credits` still buys exactly one
   39:  * pack and the debit still refuses (the user buys the rest manually). Taking
   40:  * the argument without acting on its magnitude is deliberate â€” the alternative
   41:  * reading, "buy as many packs as it takes", is the one F4 rejected.
   42:  */
   43: export async function maybeAutoTopup(
   44:   db: DbLike,
   45:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   46:   shortfall: number,
   47:   at: Date
   48: ): Promise<AutoTopupResult> {
   49:   if (!Number.isInteger(shortfall) || shortfall <= 0) {
   50:     throw new Error(
   51:       `maybeAutoTopup: shortfall must be a positive integer number of credits (got ${shortfall}) â€” it is the amount the refused debit was short by.`
   52:     );
   53:   }
   54:   const [sub] = await db
   55:     .select()
   56:     .from(subscriptions)
   57:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
   58:     .limit(1);
   59:   if (!sub) return { triggered: false, reason: "no_customer" };
   60:   // LIVENESS, through the ONE definition (billing round-7 CHANGE 1). Charging
   61:   // off-session needs a subscription that still exists in Stripe. Cancellation
   62:   // is the stronger form of the R-12 "no charges" rule the pause guard below
   63:   // already states, and it had no guard at all: an owner who enabled
   64:   // auto-top-up at a $50 cap and then self-serve cancelled left
   65:   // {status: canceled, autoTopupEnabled: true} on the mirror â€” free everywhere
   66:   // else in the product, but still armed here, so M3's debit site would charge
   67:   // a $10 off-session PaymentIntent to a customer who cancelled. Clearing the
   68:   // flag on `customer.subscription.deleted` (webhooks.ts) is the other half;
   69:   // this guard is the one that also covers a mirror that never had a
   70:   // subscription (a pack-only customer has no saved payment method to charge)
   71:   // and one whose cancellation we learned about some other way.
   72:   //
   73:   // Stated consequence: auto-top-up is a subscriber feature. A workspace with
   74:   // no live subscription buys packs through the manual Checkout, which is also
   75:   // what `setAutoTopup`'s own "subscribe first" refusal already says.
   76:   if (!hasLiveStripeSubscription(sub)) {
   77:     return { triggered: false, reason: "not_subscribed" };
   78:   }
   79:   // R-12 "no charges" while paused â€” guard in the function, not the caller.
   80:   if (sub.pausedAt !== null) return { triggered: false, reason: "paused" };
   81:   if (!sub.autoTopupEnabled || sub.autoTopupMonthlyCapCents === null) {
   82:     return { triggered: false, reason: "disabled" };
   83:   }
   84: 
   85:   const { content } = await getActiveConfig(db);
   86:   const packCents = Math.round(content.pack.priceUsd * 100);
   87: 
   88:   // Cap headroom in REAL CENTS from this-calendar-month auto-top-up rows'
   89:   // amountCents (never reconstructed from credits â€” billing round-1 finding 6).
   90:   const monthStart = new Date(
   91:     Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), at.getUTCMonth(), 1)
   92:   );
   93:   const rows = await db
   94:     .select({
   95:       cents: sql<number>`coalesce(sum(${creditLedger.amountCents}), 0)`,
   96:       n: sql<number>`count(*)`,
   97:     })
   98:     .from(creditLedger)
   99:     .where(
  100:       and(
  101:         eq(creditLedger.workspaceId, workspaceId),
  102:         eq(creditLedger.refType, "auto_topup"),
  103:         gte(creditLedger.createdAt, monthStart)
  104:       )
  105:     );
  106:   const spentCents = Number(rows[0]?.cents ?? 0);
  107:   const n = Number(rows[0]?.n ?? 0);
  108:   if (spentCents + packCents > sub.autoTopupMonthlyCapCents) {
  109:     return { triggered: false, reason: "cap_reached" };
  110:   }
  111: 
  112:   // Idempotency key dedupes concurrent duplicate triggers to ONE PaymentIntent
  113:   // (same n â†’ same key â†’ Stripe returns the same PI). Stated consequence: a
  114:   // DECLINED off-session PI replays its decline under the same key until the
  115:   // month's row count changes â€” fail-safe; manual pack checkout is the
  116:   // recovery path (billing plan-gate round-2 note).
  117:   const yyyyMm = `${at.getUTCFullYear()}-${String(at.getUTCMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  118:   const idempotencyKey = `autotopup:${workspaceId}:${yyyyMm}:${n + 1}`;
  119:   const pi = await getStripe().paymentIntents.create(
  120:     {
  121:       amount: packCents,
  122:       currency: "usd",
  123:       customer: sub.stripeCustomerId,
  124:       off_session: true,
  125:       confirm: true,
  126:       metadata: { respin_kind: "auto_topup", workspace_id: workspaceId },
  127:     },
  128:     { idempotencyKey }
  129:   );
  130:   // Credits land via the payment_intent.succeeded webhook (single-tx, event-id
  131:   // idempotent) â€” never here.
  132:   return { triggered: true, paymentIntentId: pi.id };
  133: }
===== respin/packages/credits/src/stripe/customers.ts =====
    1: // Stripe customer â†” workspace mapping (D-M1-6): created at checkout-session
    2: // creation, BEFORE redirect, so by webhook time the stored mapping â€” the SOLE
    3: // resolution authority â€” always exists for legitimate events.
    4: // This file is a sanctioned trustWorkspaceId import site (webhook resolution).
    5: import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
    6: import {
    7:   subscriptions,

    9:   type DbLike,
   10:   type TxLike,
   11:   type VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   12: } from "@respin/db";
   13: import { getStripe } from "./adapter";

   15: /**
   16:  * Lost the mapping insert race AND the winning row is already gone â€” a
   17:  * concurrent workspace delete. Typed (billing round-10 NOTE 1) because it is
   18:  * reachable from `createTierCheckoutUrl`/`createPackCheckoutUrl`, i.e. from the
   19:  * app-facing facade, and an anonymous Error on a payments path is one Phase 4
   20:  * cannot tell from a Stripe outage. It also carries an operator action: a live
   21:  * Stripe customer has been orphaned.
   22:  */
   23: export class CustomerMappingLostError extends Error {
   24:   /**
   25:    * IDS BELONG IN THE LOG, THE REMEDY IN THE MESSAGE (billing/tenancy round-11
   26:    * NOTE, `customers.ts:23-30`). This class is re-exported to `app/**` and
   27:    * Phase 4's billing page is what RENDERS it, so the workspace UUID and the
   28:    * Stripe customer id it used to embed would have been printed to a creator â€”
   29:    * identifiers that mean nothing to them and everything to anyone else
   30:    * reading over their shoulder or in a screenshot on a support ticket. The
   31:    * throw site logs both ids (server-side, ids-not-PII per D-M1-6) so the
   32:    * orphaned Stripe customer is still findable; the message carries only what
   33:    * the person in front of the screen can act on.
   34:    */
   35:   constructor() {
   36:     super(
   37:       "This workspace's billing record is no longer there, so the Checkout could not be started. Nothing was charged. This normally means the workspace was deleted while the page was open: reload, and if the workspace still exists, try again. If it does not, the ids needed to clean up in Stripe are in the server log."
   38:     );
   39:     this.name = "CustomerMappingLostError";
   40:   }

   43: /** Resolve a Stripe customer id to its workspace via the stored mapping. */
   44: export async function workspaceForCustomer(
   45:   db: DbLike | TxLike,
   46:   stripeCustomerId: string
   47: ): Promise<VerifiedWorkspaceId | null> {
   48:   const [row] = await db
   49:     .select({ workspaceId: subscriptions.workspaceId })
   50:     .from(subscriptions)
   51:     .where(eq(subscriptions.stripeCustomerId, stripeCustomerId))
   52:     .limit(1);
   53:   // The mapping row is written only through get-or-create below (checkout
   54:   // creation) â€” resolving through it is the sanctioned non-session mint.
   55:   return row ? trustWorkspaceId(row.workspaceId) : null;
   56: }
   57: 
   58: /**
   59:  * Get or create the Stripe customer for a workspace, persisting the mapping
   60:  * (the subscriptions row is created here with status 'none'). Upsert-on-
   61:  * conflict keeps concurrent first-checkouts single-rowed (workspace unique).
   62:  */
   63: export async function getOrCreateCustomer(
   64:   db: DbLike,
   65:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   66:   email: string
   67: ): Promise<string> {
   68:   const [existing] = await db
   69:     .select()
   70:     .from(subscriptions)
   71:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
   72:     .limit(1);
   73:   if (existing) return existing.stripeCustomerId;
   74: 
   75:   const customer = await getStripe().customers.create({
   76:     email,
   77:     metadata: { workspace_id: workspaceId },
   78:   });
   79:   const [row] = await db
   80:     .insert(subscriptions)
   81:     .values({ workspaceId, stripeCustomerId: customer.id, status: "none" })
   82:     .onConflictDoNothing({ target: subscriptions.workspaceId })
   83:     .returning();
   84:   if (row) return row.stripeCustomerId;
   85:   // Lost a concurrent race â€” the winner's mapping is authoritative.
   86:   const [winner] = await db
   87:     .select()
   88:     .from(subscriptions)
   89:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
   90:     .limit(1);
   91:   if (!winner) {
   92:     // Lost the insert race AND the winning row is already gone (a concurrent
   93:     // workspace delete). Say that, rather than dereferencing undefined and
   94:     // reporting a TypeError from a payments path (code-review NOTE).
   95:     // The IDS go here â€” never into the rendered message (round-11 NOTE).
   96:     console.warn(
   97:       `[stripe-customers] mapping lost for workspace ${workspaceId}: the subscriptions row vanished after losing the insert race (concurrent workspace delete). Stripe customer ${customer.id} is now orphaned and should be deleted in the Stripe dashboard.`
   98:     );
   99:     throw new CustomerMappingLostError();
  100:   }
  101:   // The customer we just created is now an ORPHAN: it exists in Stripe with
  102:   // metadata.workspace_id but is absent from the mapping, so any event it
  103:   // emits refuses (fails closed) â€” it is still a live customer nobody will
  104:   // ever reconcile. Deleting it here would be a destructive external write on
  105:   // a race path, so instead name it loudly enough to be cleaned up
  106:   // (code-review NOTE). Ids only â€” never payloads.
  107:   if (winner.stripeCustomerId !== customer.id) {
  108:     console.warn(
  109:       `[stripe-customers] orphaned Stripe customer ${customer.id} for workspace ${workspaceId}: lost the mapping race to ${winner.stripeCustomerId}. It is unmapped (its events fail closed) and should be deleted in the Stripe dashboard.`
  110:     );
  111:   }
  112:   return winner.stripeCustomerId;
  113: }
===== respin/packages/credits/src/stripe/setup.ts =====
    1: // Checked-in Stripe setup script (build-plan M1): idempotently creates the
    2: // product + 3 recurring tier prices + 1 one-off pack price, looked up by
    3: // lookup_key so re-runs create nothing. It PRINTS the price ids and the exact

    6: // Run: pnpm stripe:setup   (requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and DATABASE_URL)
    7: //
    8: // It is also the DIVERGENCE CHECK for the one price that has two authorities:
    9: // the pack. Re-running it refuses if the Stripe pack price and the active
   10: // config's `pack.priceUsd` disagree (billing round-7 CHANGE 4).

   12: import { getActiveConfig } from "@respin/config";
   13: import { getStripe } from "./adapter";

   15: const LOOKUP = {
   16:   creator: "respin_creator_monthly",
   17:   pro: "respin_pro_monthly",
   18:   studio: "respin_studio_monthly",
   19:   pack: "respin_pack_1000",
   20: } as const;
   21: 
   22: // Launch defaults (R-7) for the three SUBSCRIPTION prices â€” indicative, and
   23: // the only authority for them: config maps a Stripe price id to a tier and to
   24: // an allowance, never to a subscription price (Stripe charges the subscription,

   29: // builds itself), while the manual pack Checkout charges the Stripe price

   32: // manual checkout still charges $10 while auto-top-up silently charges $15
   33: // off-session for the same credits, a price the user was never shown. The pack
   34: // amount now comes from config below, and a disagreement is a refusal.
   35: const TIER_AMOUNTS_CENTS = { creator: 1000, pro: 6000, studio: 20000 };

   37: export async function stripeSetup(db: DbLike): Promise<void> {
   38:   const key = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
   39:   if (!key) {
   40:     console.error(
   41:       "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set. Get a test-mode secret key from the Stripe dashboard and run:\n  STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... pnpm stripe:setup"
   42:     );
   43:     process.exitCode = 1;
   44:     return;
   45:   }
   46:   // Through the ONE factory, so AC-9 â€” which requires the Stripe client to be
   47:   // constructed only inside getStripe â€” is literally true rather than
   48:   // true-in-spirit. This script building its own client was a second
   49:   // construction site that the acceptance rule's own scan finds every time
   50:   // (billing review evidence gap 4), and it is now enforced by a test rather
   51:   // than by remembering to grep. The env check above still runs first so the
   52:   // operator gets this script's own remedy â€” the exact command to re-run â€”
   53:   // instead of the generic adapter error; getStripe would refuse identically
   54:   // a line later.
   55:   const stripe = getStripe();
   56: 
   57:   // The pack price comes from the ACTIVE CONFIG, which is the same authority
   58:   // `maybeAutoTopup` charges from. Read before any Stripe write, so a missing
   59:   // or invalid config refuses before this script creates anything.
   60:   const { version, content } = await getActiveConfig(db);
   61:   const packCents = Math.round(content.pack.priceUsd * 100);
   62: 
   63:   const products = await stripe.products.list({ limit: 100 });
   64:   let product = products.data.find((p) => p.name === "Respin");
   65:   if (!product) {
   66:     product = await stripe.products.create({ name: "Respin" });
   67:     console.log(`created product ${product.id}`);
   68:   } else {
   69:     console.log(`product exists: ${product.id}`);
   70:   }
   71: 
   72:   const existing = await stripe.prices.list({
   73:     lookup_keys: Object.values(LOOKUP) as string[],
   74:     limit: 10,
   75:   });
   76:   const byLookup = new Map(existing.data.map((p) => [p.lookup_key, p]));
   77: 
   78:   const results: Record<string, string> = {};
   79:   const amounts: Record<string, number | null> = {};
   80:   for (const tier of ["creator", "pro", "studio"] as const) {
   81:     let price = byLookup.get(LOOKUP[tier]);
   82:     if (!price) {
   83:       price = await stripe.prices.create({
   84:         product: product.id,
   85:         lookup_key: LOOKUP[tier],
   86:         currency: "usd",
   87:         unit_amount: TIER_AMOUNTS_CENTS[tier],
   88:         recurring: { interval: "month" },
   89:         nickname: `Respin ${tier} (monthly)`,
   90:       });
   91:       console.log(`created ${tier} price ${price.id} at ${TIER_AMOUNTS_CENTS[tier]}c`);
   92:     } else if (price.unit_amount !== TIER_AMOUNTS_CENTS[tier]) {
   93:       // NOT a refusal, unlike the pack (billing round-10 NOTE 5). The pack has
   94:       // TWO charging authorities â€” the Stripe price object for manual
   95:       // checkout and config's `pack.priceUsd` for the off-session
   96:       // auto-top-up PaymentIntent â€” so a divergence there really does charge
   97:       // two different prices for the same credits, and must stop the run. A
   98:       // TIER price has exactly one charger: Stripe itself. `stripePriceMap`
   99:       // records price-id â†’ tier, never an amount, so nothing in this codebase
  100:       // can disagree with what Stripe charges.
  101:       //
  102:       // What IS worth saying out loud is that the literal below (R-7 launch
  103:       // defaults, and the only authority for the SEEDED amount) no longer
  104:       // describes what this lookup_key charges â€” someone changed the price in
  105:       // the dashboard, or this script seeded it at a different figure long
  106:       // ago. Until now that was undetectable: the script printed a price id
  107:       // with no amount beside it, so an operator pasting the map into
  108:       // /admin/config could map a $10 tier onto a $60 price and see nothing.
  109:       console.warn(
  110:         `WARNING: Stripe ${tier} price ${price.id} (lookup_key ${LOOKUP[tier]}) charges ${price.unit_amount ?? "null"}c, but this script's R-7 launch default for ${tier} is ${TIER_AMOUNTS_CENTS[tier]}c. Stripe is the only charger for a subscription tier, so this is NOT a two-authority divergence like the pack and nothing is refused â€” but check that the amount below is the one you mean to sell before pasting the map.`
  111:       );
  112:     }
  113:     results[price.id] = tier;
  114:     amounts[price.id] = price.unit_amount ?? null;
  115:   }
  116:   let packPrice = byLookup.get(LOOKUP.pack);
  117:   if (!packPrice) {
  118:     packPrice = await stripe.prices.create({
  119:       product: product.id,
  120:       lookup_key: LOOKUP.pack,
  121:       currency: "usd",
  122:       // From config, never a literal â€” the manual pack Checkout charges THIS
  123:       // object while auto-top-up charges config directly, so they must be one
  124:       // number by construction.
  125:       unit_amount: packCents,
  126:       nickname: `Respin ${content.pack.credits.toLocaleString("en-US")}-credit pack`,
  127:     });
  128:     console.log(
  129:       `created pack price ${packPrice.id} at ${packCents}c (config v${version} pack.priceUsd=${content.pack.priceUsd})`
  130:     );
  131:   } else if (packPrice.unit_amount !== packCents) {
  132:     // THE DIVERGENCE CHECK, and the reason this script is worth re-running: a
  133:     // Stripe price's amount is IMMUTABLE (verified against the installed SDK â€”
  134:     // `PriceUpdateParams` has no `unit_amount`), so config drifting away from
  135:     // it cannot be repaired by an update, and the two charging paths would
  136:     // quietly disagree until a customer noticed. Refuse, and name both numbers.
  137:     throw new Error(
  138:       `PRICE DIVERGENCE: Stripe pack price ${packPrice.id} (lookup_key ${LOOKUP.pack}) charges ${packPrice.unit_amount ?? "null"}c, but the active config v${version} says pack.priceUsd=${content.pack.priceUsd} (${packCents}c). The manual pack Checkout charges the Stripe price; auto-top-up charges the config amount off-session â€” so right now the same 1,000 credits cost two different prices depending on how they are bought. A Stripe price amount cannot be updated. REMEDY, pick one: (a) set pack.priceUsd back to ${(packPrice.unit_amount ?? 0) / 100} in /admin/config; or (b) create a NEW Stripe price at ${packCents}c (\`transfer_lookup_key: true\` moves ${LOOKUP.pack} onto it) and then map the NEW price id as "pack" in stripePriceMap â€” the map is keyed by price id, so leaving the old id mapped keeps charging the old amount. Nothing was changed in Stripe by this run`
  139:     );
  140:   } else {
  141:     console.log(
  142:       `pack price ${packPrice.id} agrees with config v${version} (${packCents}c)`
  143:     );
  144:   }
  145:   results[packPrice.id] = "pack";
  146:   amounts[packPrice.id] = packPrice.unit_amount ?? null;
  147: 
  148:   console.log("\nNEXT STEP â€” paste this into /admin/config as `stripePriceMap`:");
  149:   console.log(JSON.stringify(results, null, 2));
  150:   // The amounts are printed BESIDE the map, never inside it: `stripePriceMap`
  151:   // is price-id â†’ tier by design (B5/R-7), and adding a number to it would
  152:   // create the second price authority this file argues against. They are here
  153:   // so the operator can SEE what each id charges before pasting.
  154:   console.log("\nfor reference â€” what each of those price ids charges today:");
  155:   for (const [id, tier] of Object.entries(results)) {
  156:     console.log(`  ${id}  ${tier}  ${amounts[id] ?? "null"}c`);
  157:   }
  158:   console.log(
  159:     "\nRe-run this script after any change to pack.priceUsd: it is the check that the Stripe pack price and the config price still agree."
  160:   );
  161: }

   33: export class DuplicateStripeEvent extends Error {
   34:   constructor(public readonly eventId: string) {
   35:     super(`Stripe event ${eventId} already has a final outcome`);
   36:     this.name = "DuplicateStripeEvent";
   37:   }

   39: 
   40: // Only these two constraints mean "already processed". ANY other unique
   41: // violation is a real error that must reach the route as a 500 so Stripe
   42: // redelivers â€” collapsing them all into a 200 silently discards events
   43: // (code-review BLOCK: pause_periods_open_uq / subscriptions_subscription_uq /
