   45: const IDEMPOTENCY_CONSTRAINTS = ["stripe_events_pkey", "credit_ledger_stripe_event_uq"];
   46: 
   47: // Invoices that carry a service period and therefore a monthly allowance.
   48: const GRANT_BILLING_REASONS = new Set(["subscription_create", "subscription_cycle"]);
   49: // Subscription statuses whose arrival should clear nothing but stale grace.
   50: const ACTIVE_STATUSES = new Set(["active", "trialing"]);
   51: // End states. A subscription in one of these is DEAD: no invoice, however
   52: // late, may lift it back to a paid tier (code-review BLOCK â€” resurrection).
   53: const TERMINAL_STATUSES = new Set(["canceled", "incomplete_expired", "unpaid"]);
   54: // IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES (imported from state.ts, the ONE definition) is the
   55: // subset used by the subscription-mirror guard. `unpaid` belongs in
   56: // TERMINAL_STATUSES above â€” no invoice may lift it back to a paid tier â€” but it
   57: // is NOT irreversible on the subscription itself: the installed SDK says of it
   58: // "After receiving updated payment information from a customer, you may choose
   59: // to reopen and pay their closed invoices" (stripe@22.5.0 Subscriptions.d.ts).
   60: // Using the full terminal set on the mirror writer made an `unpaid` workspace
   61: // unrecoverable by ANY event, which is a worse failure than the resurrection
   62: // the guard exists to stop (billing round-5 CHANGE). Cancellation and expiry
   63: // really are one-way; dunning is not.
   64: 
   65: /**
   66:  * Resolve the Stripe customer id for ANY event class. For `customer.*` events
   67:  * the object IS the customer (it has no `customer` field) â€” missing that made
   68:  * those events unattributable, dropping resolvable creator PII out of the
   69:  * REQ-A04 deletion cascade (code-review BLOCK).
   70:  */
   71: function customerIdOf(event: Stripe.Event): string | null {
   72:   const obj = event.data.object as {
   73:     object?: string;
   74:     id?: string;
   75:     customer?: unknown;
   76:   };
   77:   if (obj.object === "customer") {
   78:     return typeof obj.id === "string" ? obj.id : null;
   79:   }
   80:   if (typeof obj.customer === "string") return obj.customer;
   81:   // An expanded customer object on a non-customer event.
   82:   const expanded = obj.customer as { id?: string } | null | undefined;
   83:   return typeof expanded?.id === "string" ? expanded.id : null;
   84: }
   85: 
   86: /**
   87:  * The RECURRING subscription line items â€” the authority for BOTH service
   88:  * period and price. Never `lines.data[0]`, and never merely "the first
   89:  * subscription line".
   90:  *
   91:  * This selector has been wrong twice, the same way each time, so the reasoning
   92:  * is written down. `invoice.period_end` is not the service period (SDK: "the
   93:  * latest timestamp at which invoice items can be associated with this
   94:  * invoice"). Position is not the discriminator either â€” the SDK documents
   95:  * `lines` as sorted with pending invoice items INCLUDING PRORATIONS first. And
   96:  * `parent.type === "subscription_item_details"` is STILL not enough, because a
   97:  * subscription proration is exactly that shape: the installed SDK gives
   98:  * `Parent.SubscriptionItemDetails` its own `proration: boolean`, and
   99:  * Invoices.d.ts says the recommended way to find prorations is to look for
  100:  * line items where `parent.subscription_item_details.proration` is true. So on
  101:  * the renewal after any portal plan switch, a proration-blind selector still
  102:  * priced the allowance and the expiry off the wrong line (code-review BLOCK,
  103:  * three rounds running).
  104:  *
  105:  * Returns ALL matches so the caller can fail closed on an ambiguous invoice
  106:  * rather than silently picking one â€” an M1 subscription has exactly one item.
  107:  */
  108: function subscriptionLinesOf(invoice: Stripe.Invoice): Stripe.InvoiceLineItem[] {
  109:   return (invoice.lines?.data ?? []).filter(
  110:     (l) =>
  111:       l.parent?.type === "subscription_item_details" &&
  112:       l.parent.subscription_item_details?.proration !== true
  113:   );
  114: }
  115: 
  116: /**
  117:  * The fields a DEAD subscription must leave behind â€” applied by EVERY writer
  118:  * that lands an irreversible status, not just by `customer.subscription.deleted`
  119:  * (billing round-7 CHANGE 1 + NOTE 1; CLAUDE.md 2026-07-30 "fix the class, not
  120:  * the field"). A dead subscription emits no further events, so whatever this
  121:  * row says after it dies is what every later reader inherits forever:
  122:  *
  123:  *  - `cancelAtPeriodEnd`: the installed SDK documents this as "whether this
  124:  *    subscription will (if status=active) or DID (if status=canceled) cancel at
  125:  *    the end of the current billing period" (stripe@22.5.0
  126:  *    resources/Subscriptions.d.ts) â€” so a trailing `customer.subscription.
  127:  *    updated` carrying `{status: canceled, cancel_at_period_end: true}` is a
  128:  *    REAL payload shape, and mirroring it verbatim re-wrote the flag the
  129:  *    `deleted` branch had just cleared, seconds later. Phase 4's billing UI is
  130:  *    the next reader.
  131:  *  - `graceExpiresAt`: a stale dunning deadline on a dead subscription was the
  132:  *    trigger a late `invoice.paid` used to revive on.
  133:  *  - `autoTopupEnabled` / `autoTopupMonthlyCapCents`: an off-session charging
  134:  *    authority. Left armed, a workspace that cancelled still had M3's debit
  135:  *    site able to charge it a $10 pack. Stated consequence, deliberately the
  136:  *    safe direction: the opt-in does not survive a cancellation â€” a
  137:  *    re-subscribing owner opts in again.
  138:  */
  139: const DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS = {
  140:   cancelAtPeriodEnd: false,
  141:   // Same reasoning as the boolean, for the field the PORTAL actually sets
  142:   // (evidence-run finding 1): a dead subscription has no future cancellation
  143:   // date, and whatever this row says after it dies is inherited forever.
  144:   cancelAt: null,
  145:   graceExpiresAt: null,
  146:   autoTopupEnabled: false,
  147:   autoTopupMonthlyCapCents: null,
  148: } as const;
  149: 
  150: /**
  151:  * Is there a grace window still RUNNING? The never-EXTEND rule keys on this
  152:  * rather than on "a deadline column is non-null" (billing round-6 CHANGE): a
  153:  * LAPSED deadline from a previous dunning episode is not a window, and reading
  154:  * it as one made the next episode inherit an expired date â€” state.ts then
  155:  * derives `free` immediately, skipping REQ-G06's window entirely. Scoping the
  156:  * rule this way also means nothing ever has to CLEAR the deadline to make the
  157:  * next episode work, which is what removed the race the same gate found.
  158:  */
  159: function hasLiveGrace(deadline: Date | null | undefined, now: Date): boolean {
  160:   return deadline != null && deadline.getTime() > now.getTime();
  161: }
  162: 
  163: /** The statuses a running dunning episode leaves on the mirror. */
  164: const DUNNING_STATUSES = new Set(["past_due"]);
  165: 
  166: /**
  167:  * Does the deadline on the mirror belong to the CURRENT dunning episode â€” i.e.
  168:  * is this failure a continuation rather than a new one? (billing round-7 NOTE.)
  169:  *
  170:  * "Never EXTEND a live deadline" is right WITHIN an episode and wrong ACROSS
  171:  * two: a recovery seen only as `customer.subscription.updated â†’ active`
  172:  * (Stripe voided the failed invoice, so no `invoice.paid` ever arrives) leaves
  173:  * the old deadline behind, and the next dunning episode then inherited whatever
  174:  * was left of it â€” the customer gets less than the `graceDays` REQ-G06
  175:  * promises, possibly minutes. Keying "is this the same episode" on the mirror's
  176:  * STATUS rather than on the deadline's mere existence fixes that without
  177:  * reintroducing the clear round 6 removed: an `active`/`trialing` mirror means
  178:  * the previous episode ended, whoever ended it, so a fresh window opens; a
  179:  * `past_due` mirror with a live deadline means we are still inside the episode
  180:  * that opened it, so it is never extended. Nothing has to be cleared and there
  181:  * is no cross-writer race to lose â€” which is exactly why round 6 removed the
  182:  * clear in the first place.
  183:  */
  184: function inheritsGrace(
  185:   mirror: { status: string; graceExpiresAt: Date | null } | undefined,
  186:   now: Date
  187: ): boolean {
  188:   return (
  189:     mirror !== undefined &&
  190:     DUNNING_STATUSES.has(mirror.status) &&
  191:     hasLiveGrace(mirror.graceExpiresAt, now)
  192:   );
  193: }
  194: 
  195: /** Did a SUBSCRIPTION generate this invoice? One-off invoices never touch the mirror. */
  196: function isSubscriptionInvoice(invoice: Stripe.Invoice): boolean {
  197:   return invoice.parent?.subscription_details != null;
  198: }
  199: 
  200: /**
  201:  * May an INVOICE event write subscription status?
  202:  *
  203:  * Two guards, both learned the hard way, and they belong together because
  204:  * every invoice-driven status write needs both:
  205:  *
  206:  *  - TERMINAL: a canceled / incomplete_expired / unpaid subscription is dead.
  207:  *    Round 3 applied this to `invoice.paid` only, which left a two-event path
  208:  *    open: Stripe emits `invoice.payment_failed` and
  209:  *    `customer.subscription.deleted` together at the end of dunning with no
  210:  *    ordering guarantee, so a late `payment_failed` wrote `past_due` + a fresh
  211:  *    grace deadline onto a canceled workspace â€” handing back the paid tier AND
  212:  *    making the mirror non-terminal, so the next late `invoice.paid` then
  213:  *    revived it permanently (code-review BLOCK).
  214:  *  - ORDER: an invoice event older than the mirror's last subscription
  215:  *    snapshot has a stale opinion about status.
  216:  *
  217:  * Note what this does NOT do: stamp `mirrorEventAt`. That watermark means
  218:  * "the mirror reflects the subscription as of this moment", and an invoice
  219:  * event is not a subscription snapshot â€” stamping it from a partial write is
  220:  * exactly the regression BLOCK 4 records.
  221:  */
  222: function invoiceMayWriteStatus(
  223:   mirror: { status: string; mirrorEventAt: Date | null } | undefined,
  224:   event: Stripe.Event
  225: ): boolean {
  226:   if (!mirror) return false;
  227:   if (TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(mirror.status)) return false;
  228:   const eventAt = new Date(event.created * 1000);
  229:   return !(
  230:     mirror.mirrorEventAt && mirror.mirrorEventAt.getTime() > eventAt.getTime()
  231:   );
  232: }
  233: 
  234: function priceIdOfLine(line: Stripe.InvoiceLineItem | undefined): string | null {
  235:   const price = line?.pricing?.price_details?.price;
  236:   if (typeof price === "string") return price;
  237:   return typeof price === "object" && price !== null && "id" in price
  238:     ? (price as { id: string }).id
  239:     : null;
  240: }
  241: 
  242: /**
  243:  * Handle one verified Stripe event. Returns the recorded outcome; throws on
  244:  * handler failure (the route turns that into a non-2xx so Stripe retries) and
  245:  * DuplicateStripeEvent when the event already has a final outcome (â†’ 200).
  246:  */
  247: export async function handleStripeEvent(
  248:   db: DbLike,
  249:   event: Stripe.Event
  250: ): Promise<StripeEventOutcome> {
  251:   try {
  252:     return await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
  253:       const [existing] = await tx
  254:         .select({ outcome: stripeEvents.outcome })
  255:         .from(stripeEvents)
  256:         .where(eq(stripeEvents.id, event.id))
  257:         .limit(1);
  258:       if (existing) throw new DuplicateStripeEvent(event.id);
  259: 
  260:       const customerId = customerIdOf(event);
  261:       const workspaceId = customerId
  262:         ? await workspaceForCustomer(tx, customerId)
  263:         : null;
  264: 
  265:       const outcome = await dispatch(tx, event, workspaceId);
  266:       if (outcome !== "processed") {
  267:         // Payload-free refusal log (D-M1-6): id + outcome only.
  268:         console.warn(`[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} â†’ ${outcome}`);
  269:       }
  270:       const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  271:       await tx.insert(stripeEvents).values({
  272:         id: event.id,
  273:         type: event.type,
  274:         payload: event as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,
  275:         // Receipt-time attribution regardless of outcome: attributed rows join
  276:         // the REQ-A04 deletion cascade; only genuinely unattributable rows are
  277:         // left to the M6 retention sweep.
  278:         workspaceId,
  279:         stripeCustomerId: customerId,
  280:         outcome,
  281:         processedAt: now,
  282:       });
  283:       return outcome;
  284:     });
  285:   } catch (err) {
  286:     if (err instanceof DuplicateStripeEvent) throw err;
  287:     // A concurrent duplicate loses the idempotency constraint AFTER the winner
  288:     // commits; its tx rolled back completely.
  289:     if (isIdempotencyViolation(err)) throw new DuplicateStripeEvent(event.id);
  290:     throw err;
  291:   }
  292: }
  293: 
  294: function isIdempotencyViolation(err: unknown): boolean {
  295:   const e = err as {
  296:     code?: string;
  297:     constraint?: string;
  298:     cause?: { code?: string; constraint?: string };
  299:   };
  300:   const code = e?.code ?? e?.cause?.code;
  301:   if (code !== "23505") return false;
  302:   const constraint = e?.constraint ?? e?.cause?.constraint;
  303:   if (constraint) return IDEMPOTENCY_CONSTRAINTS.includes(constraint);
  304:   // Driver didn't surface the constraint name: fall back to the message, and
  305:   // if that is inconclusive treat it as a REAL error (fail closed â†’ retry).
  306:   const message = err instanceof Error ? `${err.message} ${String(err.cause ?? "")}` : "";
  307:   return IDEMPOTENCY_CONSTRAINTS.some((c) => message.includes(c));
  308: }
  309: 
  310: async function dispatch(
  311:   tx: TxLike,
  312:   event: Stripe.Event,
  313:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId | null
  314: ): Promise<StripeEventOutcome> {
  315:   switch (event.type) {
  316:     case "checkout.session.completed":
  317:     case "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded": {
  318:       const session = event.data.object as Stripe.Checkout.Session;
  319:       if (!workspaceId) return "refused_unknown_customer";
  320:       // Metadata is a CROSS-CHECK only (D-M1-6): present-and-mismatched refuses.
  321:       const metaWs = session.metadata?.workspace_id;
  322:       if (metaWs && metaWs !== workspaceId) return "refused_identity_mismatch";
  323: 
  324:       if (session.mode === "payment" && session.metadata?.respin_kind === "pack") {
  325:         // The session completing is NOT the money arriving: delayed-notification
  326:         // methods complete as `unpaid` and settle later on
  327:         // checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded (code-review BLOCK).
  328:         if (session.payment_status !== "paid") {
  329:           // 'no_payment_required' (a 100%-off or zero-amount session) would
  330:           // also land here and mint nothing forever, so say which it was
  331:           // rather than logging a bare "ignored" (code-review NOTE).
  332:           console.warn(
  333:             `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} pack session ${session.id} not minted: payment_status=${session.payment_status}`
  334:           );
  335:           return "ignored";
  336:         }
  337:         // ONE pack per SESSION, not per event id (code-review BLOCK): both
  338:         // checkout.session.completed and .async_payment_succeeded can carry
  339:         // the same session under DIFFERENT event ids, which the event-id
  340:         // unique cannot dedupe. Pre-check here so the second one converges to
  341:         // "ignored"; credit_ledger_checkout_session_uq is the guarantee if two
  342:         // land concurrently (that 23505 is not an idempotency constraint, so
  343:         // it propagates and Stripe redelivers).
  344:         const [already] = await tx
  345:           .select({ id: creditLedger.id })
  346:           .from(creditLedger)
  347:           .where(
  348:             and(
  349:               // Workspace-scoped like every other query in this package
  350:               // (tenancy T1) â€” the resolved workspace is the only one whose
  351:               // rows may answer this question. The index behind it is
  352:               // deliberately global; see billing-schema.ts for why.
  353:               eq(creditLedger.workspaceId, workspaceId),
  354:               eq(creditLedger.refType, "checkout_session"),
  355:               eq(creditLedger.refId, session.id)
  356:             )
  357:           )
  358:           .limit(1);
  359:         if (already) {
  360:           console.warn(
  361:             `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} pack session ${session.id} already minted â€” ignoring the second settlement event`
  362:           );
  363:           return "ignored";
  364:         }
  365:         const { version, content } = await getActiveConfig(tx);
  366:         const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  367:         await purchasePackCredits(tx, {
  368:           workspaceId,
  369:           amount: content.pack.credits,
  370:           expiresAt: addMonthsUtc(now, content.pack.validityMonths),
  371:           amountCents: session.amount_total ?? Math.round(content.pack.priceUsd * 100),
  372:           stripeEventId: event.id,
  373:           refType: "checkout_session",
  374:           refId: session.id,
  375:           configVersion: version,
  376:         });
  377:         return "processed";
  378:       }
  379: 
  380:       if (session.mode === "subscription") {
  381:         // `subscription` is an id or an expanded object depending on the
  382:         // request that produced the session â€” both shapes are handled and
  383:         // both are now tested (code-review CHANGE: this branch had none).
  384:         const subId =
  385:           typeof session.subscription === "string"
  386:             ? session.subscription
  387:             : (session.subscription?.id ?? null);
  388:         if (subId) {
  389:           // Order-guarded (a redelivered older checkout event must not repoint
  390:           // the mirror at a dead subscription, after which pause/resume/portal
  391:           // act on the wrong Stripe object) â€” but deliberately NOT stamping.
  392:           //
  393:           // Round 3 both guarded AND stamped here, which was a regression
  394:           // (code-review BLOCK): this branch writes only `stripeSubscriptionId`,
  395:           // so stamping the shared watermark from that PARTIAL write let a
  396:           // checkout event with a later `created` second suppress the real
  397:           // `customer.subscription.created` that follows it. The mirror then
  398:           // never records price, status or period â€” the workspace derives to
  399:           // `free` while paying, and `createTierCheckoutUrl` sees no live
  400:           // subscription, so the F1 double-billing guard silently switches off.
  401:           // The watermark belongs to full subscription snapshots only.
  402:           const eventAt = new Date(event.created * 1000);
  403:           const [mirror] = await tx
  404:             .select()
  405:             .from(subscriptions)
  406:             .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  407:             .limit(1);
  408:           if (
  409:             mirror?.mirrorEventAt &&
  410:             mirror.mirrorEventAt.getTime() > eventAt.getTime()
  411:           ) {
  412:             return "ignored";
  413:           }
  414:           // While the mirrored subscription is DEAD, this branch may not
  415:           // repoint it â€” only a full subscription snapshot may (billing
  416:           // round-5 BLOCK, reproduced by the gate). `stripeSubscriptionId` is
  417:           // what the mirror writer's irreversibility guard identifies the dead
  418:           // subscription BY, and this partial write could overwrite it: on a
  419:           // re-subscribe where `checkout.session.completed` beat
  420:           // `customer.subscription.created`, the mirror became
  421:           // {status: canceled, subscription: sub_NEW}, so the new
  422:           // subscription's own first snapshot looked exactly like a
  423:           // resurrection of the old one and was refused â€” forever, along with
  424:           // every later update. The workspace paid, was granted its credits by
  425:           // invoice.paid, and derived to `free` with no event that could ever
  426:           // correct it, while `isLive()` reading `canceled` also switched the
  427:           // F1 double-billing guard off. Nothing is lost by skipping: the
  428:           // `customer.subscription.created` that always follows binds the id
  429:           // AND the status together.
  430:           if (mirror && IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(mirror.status)) {
  431:             console.warn(
  432:               `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} not repointing a ${mirror.status} mirror at ${subId} from a checkout event; the subscription snapshot will bind it`
  433:             );
  434:             return "ignored";
  435:           }
  436:           await tx
  437:             .update(subscriptions)
  438:             .set({ stripeSubscriptionId: subId })
  439:             .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
  440:         }
  441:         return "processed";
  442:       }
  443:       return "ignored";
  444:     }
  445: 
  446:     case "customer.subscription.created":
  447:     case "customer.subscription.updated": {
  448:       const sub = event.data.object as Stripe.Subscription;
  449:       if (!workspaceId) return "refused_unknown_customer";
  450:       const eventAt = new Date(event.created * 1000);
  451:       const [mirror] = await tx
  452:         .select()
  453:         .from(subscriptions)
  454:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  455:         .limit(1);
  456:       // Stripe does not guarantee delivery ORDER: a stale event must never
  457:       // overwrite newer state (code-review CHANGE: order-blind mirror writes).
  458:       if (mirror?.mirrorEventAt && mirror.mirrorEventAt.getTime() > eventAt.getTime()) {
  459:         return "ignored";
  460:       }
  461:       // TERMINAL guard â€” the resurrection rule the invoice writers already
  462:       // have, which this one lacked (billing review finding 5). The order
  463:       // guard above is STRICT (`>`), so an event whose `created` second EQUALS
  464:       // the mirror's watermark is applied: `deleted` and a still-`active`
  465:       // `updated` are emitted together at the end of a subscription's life and
  466:       // routinely share a second, so whichever arrived second won â€” and if
  467:       // that was `updated`, a canceled workspace went back to a paid tier with
  468:       // no later event to correct it. Nothing in the payload can order two
  469:       // events inside one second (Stripe exposes no sequence number), so
  470:       // instead of pretending to order them this refuses the one direction
  471:       // that costs money: a DEAD subscription never returns to life.
  472:       //
  473:       // Keyed on the subscription id, so a genuine RE-subscribe â€” which always
  474:       // creates a new Stripe subscription â€” is unaffected and still mirrors.
  475:       if (
  476:         mirror &&
  477:         IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(mirror.status) &&
  478:         mirror.stripeSubscriptionId === sub.id &&
  479:         !IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(sub.status)
  480:       ) {
  481:         console.warn(
  482:           `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} would lift subscription ${sub.id} out of terminal status ${mirror.status} â†’ ${sub.status}; refusing (a dead subscription is never revived)`
  483:         );
  484:         return "ignored";
  485:       }
  486:       // Symmetric with invoice.paid's ambiguity refusal (billing review
  487:       // finding 6): the mirror priced the tier off `items.data[0]` while the
  488:       // invoice path refuses to guess between two lines. A multi-item
  489:       // subscription would silently mirror ONE of its prices, and tier is
  490:       // derived from that price at read time â€” so the workspace could be
  491:       // charged for one plan and entitled to another. M1 sells single-item
  492:       // subscriptions; there is no rule for which item is the plan.
  493:       const items = sub.items?.data ?? [];
  494:       if (items.length > 1) {
  495:         throw new Error(
  496:           `${event.type} ${event.id}: subscription ${sub.id} has ${items.length} items â€” M1 sells single-item subscriptions, so there is no rule for which item carries the plan price; refusing to mirror a guess. REMEDY: open subscription ${sub.id} in the Stripe dashboard and remove the extra item(s) so exactly one priced item remains, then the redelivery succeeds. Until then EVERY mirror update for this workspace is blocked, including pause/resume sync. Stripe will redeliver`
  497:         );
  498:       }
  499:       const item = items[0];
  500:       const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  501:       // Grace must NOT depend on delivery order (billing review finding 1).
  502:       // `invoice.payment_failed` is what normally opens the 7-day window, but
  503:       // it is order-guarded against this watermark: when Stripe delivers the
  504:       // dunning `subscription.updated` (created one second later) FIRST, the
  505:       // older payment_failed is correctly ignored â€” and the deadline it would
  506:       // have written is then never written by anyone. `past_due` with a null
  507:       // deadline derives to `free` in state.ts, so the customer lost the whole
  508:       // grace period to a delivery-order coin flip. Opening the window here
  509:       // too makes both orders converge on ONE deadline; payment_failed's own
  510:       // "never EXTEND an existing deadline" rule is what keeps it single.
  511:       //
  512:       // Round 7 narrows the "already has one" test from "a deadline exists" to
  513:       // "we are still inside the episode it belongs to" (see inheritsGrace) â€”
  514:       // otherwise a recovery seen only as `updated â†’ active` left a live
  515:       // deadline that the NEXT episode inherited, short.
  516:       const opensGrace = sub.status === "past_due" && !inheritsGrace(mirror, now);
  517:       const graceDays = opensGrace
  518:         ? (await getActiveConfig(tx)).content.graceDays
  519:         : null;
  520:       await tx
  521:         .update(subscriptions)
  522:         .set({
  523:           stripeSubscriptionId: sub.id,
  524:           stripePriceId: item?.price?.id ?? null,
  525:           status: sub.status,
  526:           currentPeriodStart: item ? new Date(item.current_period_start * 1000) : null,
  527:           currentPeriodEnd: item ? new Date(item.current_period_end * 1000) : null,
  528:           cancelAtPeriodEnd: sub.cancel_at_period_end,
  529:           // BOTH, because Stripe expresses one fact two ways and the evidence
  530:           // run proved the boolean alone is not enough: a Customer Portal
  531:           // cancellation arrived as {cancel_at: <ts>, cancel_at_period_end:
  532:           // FALSE, status: active}. `scheduledCancelAt` (state.ts) is the ONE
  533:           // reader that turns the pair into a date.
  534:           cancelAt: sub.cancel_at ? new Date(sub.cancel_at * 1000) : null,
  535:           mirrorEventAt: eventAt,
  536:           // A snapshot that lands an IRREVERSIBLE status is a death notice, and
  537:           // must leave exactly what `customer.subscription.deleted` leaves â€”
  538:           // including overriding the `cancel_at_period_end: true` the payload
  539:           // itself still carries on a canceled object (see
  540:           // DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS). Spread AFTER the payload fields so the
  541:           // death rule wins.
  542:           ...(IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(sub.status)
  543:             ? DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS
  544:             : {}),
  545:           // Grace is opened here when `past_due` arrives without a LIVE
  546:           // deadline (the order-independence fix above); it is cleared only by
  547:           // a paid invoice. Round 5 also cleared it on an ACTIVE status, which
  548:           // the round-6 gate reproduced as a hazard: `invoice.payment_failed`
  549:           // deliberately does not stamp `mirrorEventAt`, so the watermark
  550:           // carries no information about a deadline's age and the order guard
  551:           // above cannot protect it â€” an OLDER `active` snapshot wiped a live
  552:           // deadline and served the paid tier to a non-payer. The stale-across-
  553:           // episodes problem that clear was for is now solved where it belongs,
  554:           // in the never-EXTEND rule itself: an EXPIRED deadline is not a live
  555:           // one, so a later episode opens a fresh window without anyone having
  556:           // to clear anything.
  557:           ...(graceDays !== null
  558:             ? {
  559:                 graceExpiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() + graceDays * 86_400_000),
  560:               }
  561:             : {}),
  562:         })
  563:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
  564: 
  565:       // Pause mirror sync â€” convergent by construction, through the SAME
  566:       // helpers the owner action uses (pause.ts), so neither writer can throw
  567:       // at the other's ordering and the two paths cannot drift apart.
  568:       const paused = sub.pause_collection != null;
  569:       if (paused) {
  570:         const resumesAt = sub.pause_collection?.resumes_at
  571:           ? new Date(sub.pause_collection.resumes_at * 1000)
  572:           : undefined;
  573:         // `eventAt` bounds what this snapshot can know, SYMMETRICALLY with the
  574:         // ensurePauseEnded call below (billing round-10 NOTE 3): a snapshot
  575:         // created before the owner RESUMED must not re-open the pause it is
  576:         // still reporting, because `resumeSubscription` does not stamp
  577:         // `mirrorEventAt` and the order guard above therefore cannot see it.
  578:         await ensurePauseStarted(tx, workspaceId, now, resumesAt, eventAt);
  579:       } else {
  580:         // `eventAt` bounds what this snapshot can know: a pause that started
  581:         // AFTER this event was created is invisible to it, and closing it would
  582:         // silently undo an owner pause the reconciling webhook has not seen yet
  583:         // (billing round-7 NOTE â€” the pause writer and this watermark are on
  584:         // different clocks, because `pauseSubscription` deliberately does not
  585:         // stamp `mirrorEventAt`).
  586:         await ensurePauseEnded(tx, workspaceId, now, eventAt);
  587:       }
  588:       return "processed";
  589:     }
  590: 
  591:     case "customer.subscription.deleted": {
  592:       const sub = event.data.object as Stripe.Subscription;
  593:       if (!workspaceId) return "refused_unknown_customer";
  594:       const eventAt = new Date(event.created * 1000);
  595:       const [prior] = await tx
  596:         .select()
  597:         .from(subscriptions)
  598:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  599:         .limit(1);
  600:       // This was the one mirror writer that stamped the watermark without
  601:       // reading it (code-review CHANGE). A redelivered OLD `deleted` for a
  602:       // previous subscription would otherwise cancel a workspace that has
  603:       // since re-subscribed â€” and close its open pause on the way through.
  604:       if (prior?.mirrorEventAt && prior.mirrorEventAt.getTime() > eventAt.getTime()) {
  605:         return "ignored";
  606:       }
  607:       // The mirror image of the checkout guard above: a `deleted` for an OLD
  608:       // subscription must not cancel the CURRENT one. This branch writes
  609:       // `stripeSubscriptionId: sub.id` unconditionally, so without this a late
  610:       // cancellation of sub_1 â€” arriving after the workspace re-subscribed on
  611:       // sub_2, which is an ordinary flow when the cancel event is delayed â€”
  612:       // would both cancel the live subscription and repoint the mirror at the
  613:       // dead one, taking the pause with it.
  614:       if (prior?.stripeSubscriptionId && prior.stripeSubscriptionId !== sub.id) {
  615:         console.warn(
  616:           `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} cancels ${sub.id} but the mirror holds ${prior.stripeSubscriptionId}; refusing to cancel a different subscription`
  617:         );
  618:         return "ignored";
  619:       }
  620:       const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  621:       await ensurePauseEnded(tx, workspaceId, now);
  622:       await tx
  623:         .update(subscriptions)
  624:         .set({
  625:           status: "canceled",
  626:           stripeSubscriptionId: sub.id,
  627:           mirrorEventAt: new Date(event.created * 1000),
  628:           // Nothing reset these fields before round 6, and no further events
  629:           // exist for a dead subscription to reset them later â€” so whatever
  630:           // they said at death is what every later reader inherited (billing +
  631:           // tenancy round-6 BLOCK for cancelAtPeriodEnd, billing round-7
  632:           // CHANGE 1 for the auto-top-up authority). One definition, shared
  633:           // with the mirror writer above, so the two cannot drift.
  634:           ...DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS,
  635:         })
  636:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
  637:       return "processed";
  638:     }
  639: 
  640:     case "invoice.paid": {
  641:       const invoice = event.data.object as Stripe.Invoice;
  642:       if (!workspaceId) return "refused_unknown_customer";
  643:       // Cycle-only grants (plan-review F2): proration/one-off invoice.paid
  644:       // shapes are IGNORED with zero ledger writes â€” never a throw on money
  645:       // already taken. Mid-cycle upgrades grant at the next anniversary (R-20).
  646:       if (
  647:         !invoice.billing_reason ||
  648:         !GRANT_BILLING_REASONS.has(invoice.billing_reason)
  649:       ) {
  650:         return "ignored";
  651:       }
  652: 
  653:       // SERVICE period and price BOTH come from the SUBSCRIPTION line, chosen
  654:       // by discriminator (never by position â€” see subscriptionLineOf).
  655:       // invoice.period_end is "the latest timestamp at which invoice items can
  656:       // be associated with this invoice" (SDK docs) â€” creation time on a
  657:       // subscription_create invoice, which destroyed REQ-G02's rollover.
  658:       const lines = subscriptionLinesOf(invoice);
  659:       const [mirror] = await tx
  660:         .select()
  661:         .from(subscriptions)
  662:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  663:         .limit(1);
  664:       // A grant-bearing invoice with NO recurring subscription line is not a
  665:       // shape we understand: falling through would price the allowance off the
  666:       // mirror while the customer was charged for something else. Fail closed
  667:       // FIRST, so the diagnosis names the real problem, not its symptom.
  668:       if (lines.length === 0) {
  669:         throw new Error(
  670:           `invoice.paid ${event.id}: billing_reason ${invoice.billing_reason} implies a subscription allowance, but no line item is a non-proration "subscription_item_details" line â€” refusing to grant from a proration or a non-subscription line; Stripe will redeliver`
  671:         );
  672:       }
  673:       // Two recurring lines means a multi-item subscription, which M1 does not
  674:       // sell. Picking one would be a guess about which price is the allowance.
  675:       if (lines.length > 1) {
  676:         throw new Error(
  677:           `invoice.paid ${event.id}: ${lines.length} recurring subscription lines on one invoice â€” M1 sells single-item subscriptions, so there is no rule for which line carries the allowance; Stripe will redeliver`
  678:         );
  679:       }
  680:       const line = lines[0]!;
  681: 
  682:       // The service period is REQUIRED, both ends, with no fallback (billing
  683:       // review finding 8). The installed SDK types it non-nullable
  684:       // (`period: { start: number; end: number }` in InvoiceLineItems.d.ts), so
  685:       // for a genuine payload this refusal never fires â€” but the two branches
  686:       // it replaces both failed OPEN on the shape the types forbid: a missing
  687:       // `end` silently priced the expiry off `mirror.currentPeriodEnd` (which
  688:       // can belong to a DIFFERENT cycle than the invoice being paid), and a
  689:       // missing `start` skipped the monthly-interval guard entirely, handing an
  690:       // annual subscriber one month of credits â€” the exact defect BLOCKER 3
  691:       // was raised to close. Guessing an expiry is the thing this handler
  692:       // refuses to do everywhere else; it now refuses here too.
  693:       const periodStart = line.period?.start;
  694:       const periodEnd = line.period?.end;
  695:       if (typeof periodStart !== "number" || typeof periodEnd !== "number") {
  696:         throw new Error(
  697:           `invoice.paid ${event.id}: the subscription line item carries no complete service period (start=${String(periodStart)}, end=${String(periodEnd)}) â€” refusing to guess a credit expiry or to skip the monthly-interval check. The installed SDK types this field as always present, so a payload without it means the API version or the line shape has changed. REMEDY: inspect invoice ${invoice.id ?? "(no id)"} in the Stripe dashboard and compare its line items against the version pinned in adapter.ts; the allowance cannot be dated until one of the two is corrected. Stripe will redeliver`
  698:         );
  699:       }
  700:       const servicePeriodEnd = new Date(periodEnd * 1000);
  701: 
  702:       // REQ-G02 assumes a MONTHLY allowance (expiry = period end + 1 month).
  703:       // An annual price would silently hand a year's subscriber one month of
  704:       // credits, and `stripePriceMap` records tier WITHOUT interval, so config
  705:       // can already express what this code cannot honour (code-review BLOCK).

   38: export async function deriveBalanceInTx(

   30: /**

   37:  * `transaction_timestamp()`, fixed when the calling transaction began â€” so

   46:  * survived, because this was the cause.
   47:  *
   48:  * `clock_timestamp()` advances within the transaction, so every row committed
   49:  * before the lock was acquired is necessarily <= it, and the fold sees them

   55: export async function getDbNow(tx: TxLike): Promise<Date> {

   57:   // but the generic PgDatabase type erases it â€” hence the cast.

   80:   tx: TxLike,
   81:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId

  104: /** Guard for allocating writes: at within skew of DB now, never retroactive. */
  105: export async function assertWriteClock(
  106:   tx: TxLike,
  107:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
  108:   at: Date
  109: ): Promise<Date> {
  110:   const dbNow = await getDbNow(tx);
  111:   // Symmetric skew (plan text: "within 60s of DB now()"): a stale PAST `at`
  112:   // is refused even with no intervening events â€” billing round-1 note.
  113:   if (Math.abs(at.getTime() - dbNow.getTime()) > CLOCK_SKEW_MS) {
  114:     throw new ClockSkewError(
  115:       `at (${at.toISOString()}) is more than ${CLOCK_SKEW_MS / 1000}s from the database clock (${dbNow.toISOString()})`
  116:     );
  117:   }
  118:   const latest = await latestEventAt(tx, workspaceId);
  119:   // Skew allowance on BOTH sides (tenancy code-review BLOCK 1): concurrent
  120:   // legitimate writes serialize on the advisory lock, so a strict ms-exact
  121:   // comparison would refuse a contemporaneous debit whose `at` was captured
  122:   // before the previous winner committed. The guard targets STALE clocks
  123:   // (minutes/hours), not lock-serialization ordering.
  124:   if (latest && at.getTime() < latest.getTime() - CLOCK_SKEW_MS) {
  125:     throw new ClockSkewError(
  126:       `at (${at.toISOString()}) is more than ${CLOCK_SKEW_MS / 1000}s earlier than the workspace's latest recorded event (${latest.toISOString()}) â€” retroactive allocating writes are refused`
  127:     );
  128:   }
  129:   return dbNow;
  130: }

  294: function isIdempotencyViolation(err: unknown): boolean {

  298:     cause?: { code?: string; constraint?: string };

  207: /**

  216:  * The fallback covers rows written before `ended_known_at` existed, where the

  220: async function lastPauseCloseKnownAt(
  221:   tx: TxLike,
  222:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId
  223: ): Promise<Date | null> {
  224:   const closeKnownAt = sql<Date>`coalesce(${pausePeriods.endedKnownAt}, ${pausePeriods.endedAt})`;

  226:     .select({ knownAt: closeKnownAt })
  227:     .from(pausePeriods)
  228:     .where(
  229:       and(

  231:         isNotNull(pausePeriods.endedAt)
  232:       )
  233:     )
  234:     .orderBy(desc(closeKnownAt))
  235:     .limit(1);
  236:   if (!row?.knownAt) return null;
  237:   return row.knownAt instanceof Date ? row.knownAt : new Date(row.knownAt);

  266:       if (outcome !== "processed") {
  267:         // Payload-free refusal log (D-M1-6): id + outcome only.
  268:         console.warn(`[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} â†’ ${outcome}`);
  269:       }
  270:       const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  271:       await tx.insert(stripeEvents).values({
  272:         id: event.id,
  273:         type: event.type,
  274:         payload: event as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,
  275:         // Receipt-time attribution regardless of outcome: attributed rows join
  276:         // the REQ-A04 deletion cascade; only genuinely unattributable rows are
  277:         // left to the M6 retention sweep.
  278:         workspaceId,
  279:         stripeCustomerId: customerId,
  280:         outcome,
  281:         processedAt: now,
  282:       });
  283:       return outcome;
  284:     });
  285:   } catch (err) {
  286:     if (err instanceof DuplicateStripeEvent) throw err;
  287:     // A concurrent duplicate loses the idempotency constraint AFTER the winner
  288:     // commits; its tx rolled back completely.
  289:     if (isIdempotencyViolation(err)) throw new DuplicateStripeEvent(event.id);
  290:     throw err;
  291:   }
  292: }
  293: 
  294: function isIdempotencyViolation(err: unknown): boolean {
  295:   const e = err as {
  296:     code?: string;
  297:     constraint?: string;
  298:     cause?: { code?: string; constraint?: string };
  299:   };
  300:   const code = e?.code ?? e?.cause?.code;
  301:   if (code !== "23505") return false;
  302:   const constraint = e?.constraint ?? e?.cause?.constraint;
  303:   if (constraint) return IDEMPOTENCY_CONSTRAINTS.includes(constraint);
  304:   // Driver didn't surface the constraint name: fall back to the message, and
  305:   // if that is inconclusive treat it as a REAL error (fail closed â†’ retry).
  306:   const message = err instanceof Error ? `${err.message} ${String(err.cause ?? "")}` : "";
  307:   return IDEMPOTENCY_CONSTRAINTS.some((c) => message.includes(c));
  308: }
  309: 
  310: async function dispatch(
  311:   tx: TxLike,
  312:   event: Stripe.Event,
  313:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId | null
  314: ): Promise<StripeEventOutcome> {
  315:   switch (event.type) {
  316:     case "checkout.session.completed":
  317:     case "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded": {
  318:       const session = event.data.object as Stripe.Checkout.Session;
  319:       if (!workspaceId) return "refused_unknown_customer";
  320:       // Metadata is a CROSS-CHECK only (D-M1-6): present-and-mismatched refuses.
  321:       const metaWs = session.metadata?.workspace_id;
  322:       if (metaWs && metaWs !== workspaceId) return "refused_identity_mismatch";
  323: 
  324:       if (session.mode === "payment" && session.metadata?.respin_kind === "pack") {
  325:         // The session completing is NOT the money arriving: delayed-notification
  326:         // methods complete as `unpaid` and settle later on
  327:         // checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded (code-review BLOCK).
  328:         if (session.payment_status !== "paid") {
  329:           // 'no_payment_required' (a 100%-off or zero-amount session) would
  330:           // also land here and mint nothing forever, so say which it was
  331:           // rather than logging a bare "ignored" (code-review NOTE).
  332:           console.warn(
  333:             `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} pack session ${session.id} not minted: payment_status=${session.payment_status}`
  334:           );
  335:           return "ignored";
  336:         }
  337:         // ONE pack per SESSION, not per event id (code-review BLOCK): both
  338:         // checkout.session.completed and .async_payment_succeeded can carry
  339:         // the same session under DIFFERENT event ids, which the event-id
  340:         // unique cannot dedupe. Pre-check here so the second one converges to
  341:         // "ignored"; credit_ledger_checkout_session_uq is the guarantee if two
  342:         // land concurrently (that 23505 is not an idempotency constraint, so
  343:         // it propagates and Stripe redelivers).
  344:         const [already] = await tx
  345:           .select({ id: creditLedger.id })
  346:           .from(creditLedger)
  347:           .where(
  348:             and(
  349:               // Workspace-scoped like every other query in this package
  350:               // (tenancy T1) â€” the resolved workspace is the only one whose
  351:               // rows may answer this question. The index behind it is
  352:               // deliberately global; see billing-schema.ts for why.
  353:               eq(creditLedger.workspaceId, workspaceId),
  354:               eq(creditLedger.refType, "checkout_session"),
  355:               eq(creditLedger.refId, session.id)
  356:             )
  357:           )
  358:           .limit(1);
  359:         if (already) {
  360:           console.warn(
  361:             `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} pack session ${session.id} already minted â€” ignoring the second settlement event`
  362:           );
  363:           return "ignored";
  364:         }
  365:         const { version, content } = await getActiveConfig(tx);
  366:         const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  367:         await purchasePackCredits(tx, {
  368:           workspaceId,
  369:           amount: content.pack.credits,
  370:           expiresAt: addMonthsUtc(now, content.pack.validityMonths),
  371:           amountCents: session.amount_total ?? Math.round(content.pack.priceUsd * 100),
  372:           stripeEventId: event.id,
  373:           refType: "checkout_session",
  374:           refId: session.id,
  375:           configVersion: version,
  376:         });
  377:         return "processed";
  378:       }
  379: 
  380:       if (session.mode === "subscription") {
  381:         // `subscription` is an id or an expanded object depending on the
  382:         // request that produced the session â€” both shapes are handled and
  383:         // both are now tested (code-review CHANGE: this branch had none).
  384:         const subId =
  385:           typeof session.subscription === "string"
  386:             ? session.subscription
  387:             : (session.subscription?.id ?? null);
  388:         if (subId) {
  389:           // Order-guarded (a redelivered older checkout event must not repoint
  390:           // the mirror at a dead subscription, after which pause/resume/portal
  391:           // act on the wrong Stripe object) â€” but deliberately NOT stamping.
  392:           //
  393:           // Round 3 both guarded AND stamped here, which was a regression
  394:           // (code-review BLOCK): this branch writes only `stripeSubscriptionId`,
  395:           // so stamping the shared watermark from that PARTIAL write let a
  396:           // checkout event with a later `created` second suppress the real
  397:           // `customer.subscription.created` that follows it. The mirror then
  398:           // never records price, status or period â€” the workspace derives to
  399:           // `free` while paying, and `createTierCheckoutUrl` sees no live
  400:           // subscription, so the F1 double-billing guard silently switches off.
  401:           // The watermark belongs to full subscription snapshots only.
  402:           const eventAt = new Date(event.created * 1000);
  403:           const [mirror] = await tx
  404:             .select()
  405:             .from(subscriptions)
  406:             .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  407:             .limit(1);
  408:           if (
  409:             mirror?.mirrorEventAt &&
  410:             mirror.mirrorEventAt.getTime() > eventAt.getTime()
  411:           ) {
  412:             return "ignored";
  413:           }
  414:           // While the mirrored subscription is DEAD, this branch may not
  415:           // repoint it â€” only a full subscription snapshot may (billing
  416:           // round-5 BLOCK, reproduced by the gate). `stripeSubscriptionId` is
  417:           // what the mirror writer's irreversibility guard identifies the dead
  418:           // subscription BY, and this partial write could overwrite it: on a
  419:           // re-subscribe where `checkout.session.completed` beat
  420:           // `customer.subscription.created`, the mirror became
  421:           // {status: canceled, subscription: sub_NEW}, so the new
  422:           // subscription's own first snapshot looked exactly like a
  423:           // resurrection of the old one and was refused â€” forever, along with
  424:           // every later update. The workspace paid, was granted its credits by
  425:           // invoice.paid, and derived to `free` with no event that could ever
  426:           // correct it, while `isLive()` reading `canceled` also switched the
  427:           // F1 double-billing guard off. Nothing is lost by skipping: the
  428:           // `customer.subscription.created` that always follows binds the id
  429:           // AND the status together.
  430:           if (mirror && IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(mirror.status)) {
  431:             console.warn(
  432:               `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} not repointing a ${mirror.status} mirror at ${subId} from a checkout event; the subscription snapshot will bind it`
  433:             );
  434:             return "ignored";
  435:           }
  436:           await tx
  437:             .update(subscriptions)
  438:             .set({ stripeSubscriptionId: subId })
  439:             .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
  440:         }
  441:         return "processed";
  442:       }
  443:       return "ignored";
  444:     }
  445: 
  446:     case "customer.subscription.created":
  447:     case "customer.subscription.updated": {
  448:       const sub = event.data.object as Stripe.Subscription;
  449:       if (!workspaceId) return "refused_unknown_customer";
  450:       const eventAt = new Date(event.created * 1000);
  451:       const [mirror] = await tx
  452:         .select()
  453:         .from(subscriptions)
  454:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  455:         .limit(1);
  456:       // Stripe does not guarantee delivery ORDER: a stale event must never
  457:       // overwrite newer state (code-review CHANGE: order-blind mirror writes).
  458:       if (mirror?.mirrorEventAt && mirror.mirrorEventAt.getTime() > eventAt.getTime()) {
  459:         return "ignored";
  460:       }
  461:       // TERMINAL guard â€” the resurrection rule the invoice writers already
  462:       // have, which this one lacked (billing review finding 5). The order
  463:       // guard above is STRICT (`>`), so an event whose `created` second EQUALS
  464:       // the mirror's watermark is applied: `deleted` and a still-`active`
  465:       // `updated` are emitted together at the end of a subscription's life and
  466:       // routinely share a second, so whichever arrived second won â€” and if
  467:       // that was `updated`, a canceled workspace went back to a paid tier with
  468:       // no later event to correct it. Nothing in the payload can order two
  469:       // events inside one second (Stripe exposes no sequence number), so
  470:       // instead of pretending to order them this refuses the one direction
  471:       // that costs money: a DEAD subscription never returns to life.
  472:       //
  473:       // Keyed on the subscription id, so a genuine RE-subscribe â€” which always
  474:       // creates a new Stripe subscription â€” is unaffected and still mirrors.
  475:       if (
  476:         mirror &&
  477:         IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(mirror.status) &&
  478:         mirror.stripeSubscriptionId === sub.id &&
  479:         !IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(sub.status)
  480:       ) {
  481:         console.warn(
  482:           `[stripe-webhook] ${event.id} would lift subscription ${sub.id} out of terminal status ${mirror.status} â†’ ${sub.status}; refusing (a dead subscription is never revived)`
  483:         );
  484:         return "ignored";
  485:       }
  486:       // Symmetric with invoice.paid's ambiguity refusal (billing review
  487:       // finding 6): the mirror priced the tier off `items.data[0]` while the
  488:       // invoice path refuses to guess between two lines. A multi-item
  489:       // subscription would silently mirror ONE of its prices, and tier is
  490:       // derived from that price at read time â€” so the workspace could be
  491:       // charged for one plan and entitled to another. M1 sells single-item
  492:       // subscriptions; there is no rule for which item is the plan.
  493:       const items = sub.items?.data ?? [];
  494:       if (items.length > 1) {
  495:         throw new Error(
  496:           `${event.type} ${event.id}: subscription ${sub.id} has ${items.length} items â€” M1 sells single-item subscriptions, so there is no rule for which item carries the plan price; refusing to mirror a guess. REMEDY: open subscription ${sub.id} in the Stripe dashboard and remove the extra item(s) so exactly one priced item remains, then the redelivery succeeds. Until then EVERY mirror update for this workspace is blocked, including pause/resume sync. Stripe will redeliver`
  497:         );
  498:       }
  499:       const item = items[0];
  500:       const now = await getDbNow(tx);
  501:       // Grace must NOT depend on delivery order (billing review finding 1).
  502:       // `invoice.payment_failed` is what normally opens the 7-day window, but
  503:       // it is order-guarded against this watermark: when Stripe delivers the
  504:       // dunning `subscription.updated` (created one second later) FIRST, the
  505:       // older payment_failed is correctly ignored â€” and the deadline it would
  506:       // have written is then never written by anyone. `past_due` with a null
  507:       // deadline derives to `free` in state.ts, so the customer lost the whole
  508:       // grace period to a delivery-order coin flip. Opening the window here
  509:       // too makes both orders converge on ONE deadline; payment_failed's own
  510:       // "never EXTEND an existing deadline" rule is what keeps it single.
  511:       //
  512:       // Round 7 narrows the "already has one" test from "a deadline exists" to
  513:       // "we are still inside the episode it belongs to" (see inheritsGrace) â€”
  514:       // otherwise a recovery seen only as `updated â†’ active` left a live
  515:       // deadline that the NEXT episode inherited, short.
  516:       const opensGrace = sub.status === "past_due" && !inheritsGrace(mirror, now);
  517:       const graceDays = opensGrace
  518:         ? (await getActiveConfig(tx)).content.graceDays
  519:         : null;
  520:       await tx
  521:         .update(subscriptions)
  522:         .set({
  523:           stripeSubscriptionId: sub.id,
  524:           stripePriceId: item?.price?.id ?? null,
  525:           status: sub.status,
  526:           currentPeriodStart: item ? new Date(item.current_period_start * 1000) : null,
  527:           currentPeriodEnd: item ? new Date(item.current_period_end * 1000) : null,
  528:           cancelAtPeriodEnd: sub.cancel_at_period_end,
  529:           // BOTH, because Stripe expresses one fact two ways and the evidence
  530:           // run proved the boolean alone is not enough: a Customer Portal
  531:           // cancellation arrived as {cancel_at: <ts>, cancel_at_period_end:
  532:           // FALSE, status: active}. `scheduledCancelAt` (state.ts) is the ONE
  533:           // reader that turns the pair into a date.
  534:           cancelAt: sub.cancel_at ? new Date(sub.cancel_at * 1000) : null,
  535:           mirrorEventAt: eventAt,
  536:           // A snapshot that lands an IRREVERSIBLE status is a death notice, and
  537:           // must leave exactly what `customer.subscription.deleted` leaves â€”
  538:           // including overriding the `cancel_at_period_end: true` the payload
  539:           // itself still carries on a canceled object (see
  540:           // DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS). Spread AFTER the payload fields so the
  541:           // death rule wins.
  542:           ...(IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(sub.status)
  543:             ? DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS
  544:             : {}),
  545:           // Grace is opened here when `past_due` arrives without a LIVE
  546:           // deadline (the order-independence fix above); it is cleared only by
  547:           // a paid invoice. Round 5 also cleared it on an ACTIVE status, which
  548:           // the round-6 gate reproduced as a hazard: `invoice.payment_failed`
  549:           // deliberately does not stamp `mirrorEventAt`, so the watermark
  550:           // carries no information about a deadline's age and the order guard
  551:           // above cannot protect it â€” an OLDER `active` snapshot wiped a live
  552:           // deadline and served the paid tier to a non-payer. The stale-across-
  553:           // episodes problem that clear was for is now solved where it belongs,
  554:           // in the never-EXTEND rule itself: an EXPIRED deadline is not a live
  555:           // one, so a later episode opens a fresh window without anyone having
  556:           // to clear anything.
  557:           ...(graceDays !== null
  558:             ? {
  559:                 graceExpiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() + graceDays * 86_400_000),
  560:               }
  561:             : {}),
  562:         })
  563:         .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId));
  564: 
  565:       // Pause mirror sync â€” convergent by construction, through the SAME
  566:       // helpers the owner action uses (pause.ts), so neither writer can throw
  567:       // at the other's ordering and the two paths cannot drift apart.
  568:       const paused = sub.pause_collection != null;
  569:       if (paused) {
  570:         const resumesAt = sub.pause_collection?.resumes_at
  571:           ? new Date(sub.pause_collection.resumes_at * 1000)
  572:           : undefined;
  573:         // `eventAt` bounds what this snapshot can know, SYMMETRICALLY with the
  574:         // ensurePauseEnded call below (billing round-10 NOTE 3): a snapshot
  575:         // created before the owner RESUMED must not re-open the pause it is
  576:         // still reporting, because `resumeSubscription` does not stamp
  577:         // `mirrorEventAt` and the order guard above therefore cannot see it.
  578:         await ensurePauseStarted(tx, workspaceId, now, resumesAt, eventAt);
  579:       } else {
  580:         // `eventAt` bounds what this snapshot can know: a pause that started
  581:         // AFTER this event was created is invisible to it, and closing it would
  582:         // silently undo an owner pause the reconciling webhook has not seen yet
  583:         // (billing round-7 NOTE â€” the pause writer and this watermark are on
  584:         // different clocks, because `pauseSubscription` deliberately does not
  585:         // stamp `mirrorEventAt`).
  586:         await ensurePauseEnded(tx, workspaceId, now, eventAt);
  587:       }
  588:       return "processed";
  589:     }

   10: const ACTIVE_STATUSES = new Set(["active", "trialing"]);
   11: 
   12: /**
   13:  * The statuses a Stripe subscription can never come back from. Everything else
   14:  * â€” including `unpaid` and `incomplete`, which a customer can still pay out of
   15:  * â€” leaves a subscription that EXISTS in Stripe and will keep emitting events.
   16:  */
   17: export const IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES = new Set(["canceled", "incomplete_expired"]);
   18: 
   19: /**
   20:  * "Does a Stripe subscription exist for this workspace right now?" â€” the ONE
   21:  * definition, because two readers of one mirror row disagreeing is how both
   22:  * round-6 gate findings happened (billing round-6 BLOCK + CHANGE):
   23:  *
   24:  *  - `actions.ts` used to answer this with a LIVE_STATUSES allowlist that also
   25:  *    counted `cancelAtPeriodEnd` as liveness. Nothing ever resets that flag, so
   26:  *    after the ordinary REQ-G01 self-serve "cancel at period end" the mirror
   27:  *    read {canceled, cancelAtPeriodEnd: true} â€” free everywhere else, but
   28:  *    "already subscribed" here, refusing the owner a re-subscribe FOREVER and
   29:  *    pointing them at a Customer Portal with nothing left to manage.
   30:  *  - The same allowlist omitted `unpaid`, so the F1 double-billing guard waved
   31:  *    a second Checkout through for a subscription that is still alive in
   32:  *    Stripe â€” the two-subscriptions-one-workspace end state the single-row
   33:  *    mirror cannot even represent.
   34:  *
   35:  * Both disappear when liveness is derived from irreversibility rather than
   36:  * from a hand-maintained list: a subscription is live iff we have its id and
   37:  * its last known status is not one of the two it cannot return from.
   38:  */
   39: export function hasLiveStripeSubscription(row: {
   40:   stripeSubscriptionId: string | null;
   41:   status: string;
   42: }): boolean {
   43:   return (
   44:     row.stripeSubscriptionId !== null && !IRREVERSIBLE_STATUSES.has(row.status)
   45:   );
   46: }
   47: 
   48: /**
   49:  * When is this subscription scheduled to END? â€” the ONE reader of the pair of
   50:  * columns Stripe uses for one fact, for the same reason `hasLiveStripeSubscription`
   51:  * is the one reader of liveness: two callers answering it differently is how
   52:  * both round-6 findings happened.
   53:  *
   54:  * The evidence run (2026-08-17) cancelled through the Customer Portal on
   55:  * api_version 2026-05-27.dahlia and the payload carried `cancel_at: <ts>` with
   56:  * `cancel_at_period_end: FALSE` and `status: active`. A mirror reading only the
   57:  * boolean therefore stored "not cancelling" for a subscription Stripe had
   58:  * already scheduled to end, and the billing page told a paying creator nothing.
   59:  * The installed SDK documents them as different questions â€” `cancel_at` is "a
   60:  * date in the future at which the subscription will automatically get canceled",
   61:  * the boolean is "will (if status=active) or DID (if status=canceled) cancel at
   62:  * the end of the current billing period" (stripe@22.5.0
   63:  * resources/Subscriptions.d.ts:128-134) â€” so both are mirrored and read here:
   64:  *
   65:  *  - an explicit `cancelAt` wins, because it is the date Stripe will act on;
   66:  *  - the legacy boolean still resolves to the period end, so a subscription
   67:  *    cancelled through the older shape (or an older API version) is not lost;
   68:  *  - a DEAD subscription is never "scheduled to end" â€” it already has, and
   69:  *    DEAD_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS clears both columns anyway; keying on liveness
   70:  *    means a stale value cannot outlive the subscription even if it did.
   71:  */
   72: export function scheduledCancelAt(row: {
   73:   stripeSubscriptionId: string | null;
   74:   status: string;
   75:   cancelAt: Date | null;
   76:   cancelAtPeriodEnd: boolean;
   77:   currentPeriodEnd: Date | null;
   78: }): Date | null {
   79:   if (!hasLiveStripeSubscription(row)) return null;
   80:   if (row.cancelAt) return row.cancelAt;
   81:   return row.cancelAtPeriodEnd ? row.currentPeriodEnd : null;
   82: }

   84: export type BillingState = {
   85:   tier: SubscriptionTier | "free";
   86:   state: "free" | "active" | "grace" | "paused";
   87:   reason?: "unmapped_price";
   88:   graceExpiresAt?: Date;
   89:   resumesAt?: Date;
   90:   /** Set when the subscription is live but scheduled to end (REQ-G01). */
   91:   cancelAt?: Date;
   92: };

   94: export async function getWorkspaceBillingState(
   95:   db: DbLike | TxLike,
   96:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
   97:   at: Date
   98: ): Promise<BillingState> {
   99:   const [sub] = await db
  100:     .select()
  101:     .from(subscriptions)
  102:     .where(eq(subscriptions.workspaceId, workspaceId))
  103:     .limit(1);
  104:   // Free = ABSENCE of a subscriptions row (B6) â€” or a dead one.
  105:   if (!sub) return { tier: "free", state: "free" };
  106: 
  107:   const resolveTier = async (): Promise<
  108:     { tier: SubscriptionTier; reason?: undefined } | { tier: "free"; reason: "unmapped_price" }
  109:   > => {
  110:     if (!sub.stripePriceId) return { tier: "free", reason: "unmapped_price" };
  111:     const { content } = await getActiveConfig(db);

   78: /** Latest recorded event instant for the workspace (ledger + pauses). */
   79: export async function latestEventAt(
   80:   tx: TxLike,
   81:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId
   82: ): Promise<Date | null> {
   83:   const [ledgerRow] = await tx
   84:     .select({ at: creditLedger.createdAt })
   85:     .from(creditLedger)
   86:     .where(eq(creditLedger.workspaceId, workspaceId))
   87:     .orderBy(desc(creditLedger.createdAt))
   88:     .limit(1);
   89:   const [pauseRow] = await tx
   90:     .select({ started: pausePeriods.startedAt, ended: pausePeriods.endedAt })
   91:     .from(pausePeriods)
   92:     .where(eq(pausePeriods.workspaceId, workspaceId))
   93:     .orderBy(desc(pausePeriods.startedAt))
   94:     .limit(1);
   95:   const candidates = [
   96:     ledgerRow?.at,
   97:     pauseRow?.started,
   98:     pauseRow?.ended ?? undefined,
   99:   ].filter((d): d is Date => d instanceof Date);
  100:   if (candidates.length === 0) return null;
  101:   return new Date(Math.max(...candidates.map((d) => d.getTime())));
  102: }

  104: /** Guard for allocating writes: at within skew of DB now, never retroactive. */
  105: export async function assertWriteClock(
  106:   tx: TxLike,
  107:   workspaceId: VerifiedWorkspaceId,
  108:   at: Date
  109: ): Promise<Date> {
  110:   const dbNow = await getDbNow(tx);
  111:   // Symmetric skew (plan text: "within 60s of DB now()"): a stale PAST `at`
  112:   // is refused even with no intervening events â€” billing round-1 note.
  113:   if (Math.abs(at.getTime() - dbNow.getTime()) > CLOCK_SKEW_MS) {
  114:     throw new ClockSkewError(
  115:       `at (${at.toISOString()}) is more than ${CLOCK_SKEW_MS / 1000}s from the database clock (${dbNow.toISOString()})`
  116:     );
  117:   }
  118:   const latest = await latestEventAt(tx, workspaceId);
  119:   // Skew allowance on BOTH sides (tenancy code-review BLOCK 1): concurrent
  120:   // legitimate writes serialize on the advisory lock, so a strict ms-exact
  121:   // comparison would refuse a contemporaneous debit whose `at` was captured
  122:   // before the previous winner committed. The guard targets STALE clocks
  123:   // (minutes/hours), not lock-serialization ordering.
  124:   if (latest && at.getTime() < latest.getTime() - CLOCK_SKEW_MS) {
  125:     throw new ClockSkewError(
  126:       `at (${at.toISOString()}) is more than ${CLOCK_SKEW_MS / 1000}s earlier than the workspace's latest recorded event (${latest.toISOString()}) â€” retroactive allocating writes are refused`
  127:     );
  128:   }
  129:   return dbNow;
  130: }

   50: /**
   51:  * Pause-shifted effective expiry. Chronological fold per D-M1-3/D-M1-7 â€”
   52:  * counting ONLY the pause time that overlaps the lot's own lifetime
   53:  * [lotCreatedAt, shifted expiry): a clock that wasn't running yet cannot be
   54:  * suspended, so a pause that ended before the lot existed shifts nothing and
   55:  * a pause straddling the lot's creation counts only its post-creation portion
   56:  * (tenancy code-review BLOCK 2).
   57:  */
   58: export function effectiveExpiry(
   59:   expiresAt: Date | null,
   60:   pauses: PausePeriod[],
   61:   lotCreatedAt: Date
   62: ): { at: Date | null; frozen: boolean } {
   63:   if (expiresAt === null) return { at: null, frozen: false };
   64:   let eff = expiresAt.getTime();
   65:   const born = lotCreatedAt.getTime();
   66:   // Merge overlapping periods first (billing round-2 NOTE): the writer refuses
   67:   // a second open pause, but a â‰¤60s-skew overlap between adjacent periods
   68:   // would otherwise double-count the shared seconds.
   69:   const sorted = mergePauses(pauses);
   70:   for (const p of sorted) {
   71:     const overlapStart = Math.max(p.startedAt.getTime(), born);
   72:     if (overlapStart >= eff) continue; // no overlap with the lot's clock
   73:     if (p.endedAt === null) {
   74:       // Open pause overlapping the lot's lifetime before its (shifted)
   75:       // expiry: the clock is frozen â€” the lot cannot expire while paused.
   76:       return { at: null, frozen: true };
   77:     }
   78:     if (p.endedAt.getTime() <= born) continue; // ended before the lot existed
   79:     eff += p.endedAt.getTime() - overlapStart;
   80:   }
   81:   return { at: new Date(eff), frozen: false };
   82: }
   83: 
   84: /** Coalesce overlapping/touching pause intervals (open pause swallows the tail). */
   85: function mergePauses(pauses: PausePeriod[]): PausePeriod[] {
   86:   const sorted = [...pauses].sort(
   87:     (a, b) => a.startedAt.getTime() - b.startedAt.getTime()
   88:   );
   89:   const merged: PausePeriod[] = [];
   90:   for (const p of sorted) {
   91:     const last = merged[merged.length - 1];
   92:     if (
   93:       last &&
   94:       (last.endedAt === null ||
   95:         last.endedAt.getTime() >= p.startedAt.getTime())
   96:     ) {
   97:       if (last.endedAt !== null) {
   98:         const end =
   99:           p.endedAt === null
  100:             ? null
  101:             : new Date(Math.max(last.endedAt.getTime(), p.endedAt.getTime()));
  102:         merged[merged.length - 1] = { ...last, endedAt: end };
  103:       }
  104:       // last is open: it already swallows p entirely.
  105:       continue;
  106:     }
  107:     merged.push(p);
  108:   }
  109:   return merged;
  110: }

  112: function isLive(lot: LotView, t: Date): boolean {
  113:   if (lot.remaining <= 0 || lot.expiredByRow) return false;
  114:   if (lot.effectiveExpiresAt === null) return true; // never / frozen
  115:   return lot.effectiveExpiresAt.getTime() > t.getTime();
  116: }
  117: 
  118: function allocationOrder(a: LotView, b: LotView): number {
  119:   const aNever = a.effectiveExpiresAt === null;
  120:   const bNever = b.effectiveExpiresAt === null;
  121:   if (aNever !== bNever) return aNever ? 1 : -1; // never-expiring last
  122:   if (!aNever && !bNever) {
  123:     const d =
  124:       (a.effectiveExpiresAt as Date).getTime() -
  125:       (b.effectiveExpiresAt as Date).getTime();
  126:     if (d !== 0) return d; // soonest effective expiry first
  127:   }
  128:   const c = a.createdAt.getTime() - b.createdAt.getTime();
  129:   if (c !== 0) return c; // older first
  130:   return (KIND_RANK[a.kind] ?? 9) - (KIND_RANK[b.kind] ?? 9); // grants before packs
  131: }

  133: /** True for rows the fold treats as consumable lots (D-M1-7's six kinds). */
  134: function isLotRow(r: CreditLedgerRow): boolean {
  135:   return (
  136:     r.kind === "grant" ||
  137:     r.kind === "pack" ||
  138:     r.kind === "refund" ||
  139:     (r.kind === "adjust" && r.delta > 0)
  140:   );
  141: }
  142: 
  143: /**
  144:  * Replay rank for rows sharing a `created_at` to the microsecond
  145:  * (billing round-11 NOTE, `fold.ts:145-148`). The write-clock rule
  146:  * (ledger.ts) makes ties REAL, not hypothetical: expiry rows materialized by a
  147:  * fold and the debit stamped with that same fold's `asOf` carry the identical
  148:  * instant by construction. Until now the tie-break was `id.localeCompare`, i.e.
  149:  * uuidv7 order â€” true today because one process inserts the expiry rows first,
  150:  * and an assumption the moment a second backend writes in the same microsecond
  151:  * with a skewed clock. That assumption is worth removing because the failure is
  152:  * PERMANENT: replaying a debit before the lot that funded it throws
  153:  * `over-consumes`, and replaying it before its own expiry row throws
  154:  * `materialization drifted`, on a table that can never be edited to fix it.
  155:  *
  156:  * The order is the causal one, and it is the order the writers already intend:
  157:  *   0 lots (a lot must exist before anything allocates against it)
  158:  *   1 expiry (materialization claims a lot's remainder as the fold measured it)
  159:  *   2 allocating rows (debit / negative adjust)
  160:  * `id` remains the final tie-break, so ordering stays total and deterministic.
  161:  */
  162: function replayRank(r: CreditLedgerRow): number {
  163:   if (isLotRow(r)) return 0;
  164:   if (r.kind === "expiry") return 1;
  165:   return 2;
  166: }
  167: 
  168: /**
  169:  * Replay the ledger up to `asOf` (events with createdAt <= asOf) against the
  170:  * pause history. Deterministic; throws LedgerIntegrityError on history the
  171:  * schema CHECKs should have made impossible.
  172:  */
  173: export function foldLedger(
  174:   rows: CreditLedgerRow[],
  175:   pauses: PausePeriod[],
  176:   asOf: Date
  177: ): FoldResult {
  178:   const events = rows
  179:     .filter((r) => r.createdAt.getTime() <= asOf.getTime())
  180:     .sort(
  181:       (a, b) =>
  182:         a.createdAt.getTime() - b.createdAt.getTime() ||
  183:         replayRank(a) - replayRank(b) ||
  184:         a.id.localeCompare(b.id)
  185:     );
  186: 
  187:   const lots = new Map<string, LotView>();
  188:   const allocations: FoldResult["allocations"] = new Map();
  189: 
  190:   for (const ev of events) {
  191:     if (isLotRow(ev)) {
  192:       const eff = effectiveExpiry(ev.expiresAt, pauses, ev.createdAt);
  193:       lots.set(ev.id, {
  194:         id: ev.id,
  195:         kind: ev.kind,
  196:         createdAt: ev.createdAt,
  197:         expiresAt: ev.expiresAt,
  198:         effectiveExpiresAt: eff.at,
  199:         frozen: eff.frozen,
  200:         initial: ev.delta,
  201:         remaining: ev.delta,
  202:         expiredByRow: false,
  203:       });
  204:       continue;
  205:     }
  206:     if (ev.kind === "expiry") {
  207:       if (!ev.refId) {
  208:         throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  209:           `expiry row ${ev.id} names no lot (schema CHECK should forbid this)`
  210:         );
  211:       }
  212:       const lot = lots.get(ev.refId);
  213:       if (!lot) {
  214:         throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  215:           `expiry row ${ev.id} references unknown lot ${ev.refId}`
  216:         );
  217:       }
  218:       if (-ev.delta !== lot.remaining) {
  219:         throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  220:           `expiry row ${ev.id} expires ${-ev.delta} but lot ${lot.id} has ${lot.remaining} remaining â€” materialization drifted`
  221:         );
  222:       }
  223:       lot.remaining = 0;
  224:       lot.expiredByRow = true;
  225:       continue;
  226:     }
  227:     // debit, or negative adjust: allocate per D-M1-8.
  228:     const amount = -ev.delta;
  229:     if (amount <= 0) {
  230:       throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  231:         `row ${ev.id} kind ${ev.kind} has non-negative delta ${ev.delta} in the allocating branch`
  232:       );
  233:     }
  234:     const live = [...lots.values()]
  235:       .filter((l) => isLive(l, ev.createdAt))
  236:       .sort(allocationOrder);

  240:       if (toConsume === 0) break;

  242:       lot.remaining -= take;
  243:       toConsume -= take;
  244:       trace.push({ lotId: lot.id, amount: take });
  245:     }
  246:     if (toConsume > 0) {
  247:       throw new LedgerIntegrityError(
  248:         `row ${ev.id} over-consumes: ${toConsume} of ${amount} could not be allocated â€” a debit was written past the available balance`
  249:       );
  250:     }
  251:     allocations.set(ev.id, trace);
  252:   }

  256:     .filter((l) => isLive(l, asOf))
  257:     .reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.remaining, 0);
  258:   const expiryCandidates = lotViews
